SWAP HEADROOM FIX + trainer back online. The 07-05 containment (MemoryHigh=4G/MemoryMax=5G + 2G swap) proved INSUFFICIENT: OOM-kills recurred 2026-07-07 08:48Z and 2026-07-08 07:06Z (both Result: oom-kill, status=killed/15, ~40min CPU each) because the service MAIN process blew the 5G RAM + only-2G swap = ~7G effective ceiling (OOMPolicy=continue only contains a per-manifest SUBPROCESS OOM, not the orchestrator itself). The 07-08 SSH-dead escalation has CLEARED — trainer 158.178.209.121 reachable again via the relay this session (runs on issues #6003-#6006); host memory healthy (5.8G total, ~370M used, 5.2G avail) and the two OOMs were cgroup/host-ceiling kills, not a leak visible at idle. With MemorySwapMax=infinity the main process can now swap past the 5G RAM cap (13G addressable) instead of being OOM-killed; the 5G RAM cap still protects the ~6G host. Made durable in deploy/training-vm-cloud-init.yaml (runcmd provisions 8G swap idempotently) + documented in docs/ml/training-center.md. Disk after: 45G/38G used/7.8G free (83%) — acceptable, watch it. DEEPER FOLLOW-UP (the real fix, avoids swap-thrash slowdown): run each manifest in its own subprocess so the orchestrator's RSS stays low and any single manifest's OOM is fully contained by OOMPolicy=continue — currently the heavy stage lives in the main process. RESOLVED — the 8G swap fix HELD through a full nightly cycle. The cycle was still actively running (is-active=activating), grinding through market_features/market_raw dataset builds (row_count ~215838) steadily from 00:47Z → 01:20Z+ with no interruption. The proof the fix is what prevented the kill (not a lighter run): free -h showed Swap 8.0Gi total / 4.3Gi USED — the process is actively consuming 4.3G of swap, which is >2× the old 2G swap ceiling, so under the pre-fix config (5G RAM cap + 2G swap ≈ 7G) this exact run would have OOM-killed again. With MemorySwapMax=infinity the main process swaps past the 5G RAM cap instead of dying. Host mem 5.8G total / 4.6G used / 490M free (tight but stable, swap absorbing the overflow). Disk watch note stands: 45G/38G used/7.8G free (83%). The DEEPER follow-up (per-manifest subprocess isolation so the orchestrator RSS stays low and OOMPolicy=continue fully contains a single-manifest OOM — avoids the swap-thrash slowdown this fix trades for stability) remains a documented, non-urgent improvement; opening it as its own forward-looking item rather than keeping this incident item open. items.title: Trainer memory: run each manifest in its own subprocess so the orchestrator RSS stays low (avoid swap-thrash); confirm dataset_builds.jsonl path
items.description: The proper fix (deeper than the swap headroom): run each training manifest in its OWN subprocess so the orchestrator's resident set stays small and a single manifest's OOM is fully contained by the unit's OOMPolicy=continue (per-manifest subprocess kill) instead of the main process ballooning to ~9G total footprint and leaning on 4.3G of swap. That removes the swap-thrash the current fix accepts, and keeps the 5G RAM cap protecting the ~6G host without ever needing to page. Scope: identify the heavy stage that lives in the main process (the quiet 05:40-06:15 big-allocation stage from the original incident — likely a corpus/dataset build post-manifest-loop), refactor it (or the manifest loop) into a spawned subprocess per manifest, re-verify a nightly cycle stays low-RSS. SECONDARY (carried from the parent item): confirm where dataset_builds.jsonl actually lives — the original diag path check at ~/ict-trading-bot/runtime_logs/ found nothing; resolve the real path (or the writer) so dataset-build health is queryable. Trainer-VM autonomous territory (no operator gate to implement); non-urgent since the swap fix has the box stable.

updates.note: RECURRENCE — the swap-thrash tradeoff this item flagged BIT for real, elevating it from non-urgent to prioritize. 2026-07-10 ~09:34Z the trainer went SSH-DEAD (trainer_reachability_alert DOWN; trainer-vm-diag probe #6085 returned 'Connection timed out during banner exchange … port 22 timed out'). This is the swap-thrash failure mode the 8G-swap 'fix' accepts made concrete: instead of an OOM-kill the box paged so hard on the 1-OCPU trainer that sshd could not complete a handshake — the VM was alive but unreachable, so no in-band recovery was possible. RECOVERED autonomously via an OCI control-plane hard RESET (reset-instance workflow, issue #6086: STOPPING→RUNNING, capacity preserved, no terminate) — the sanctioned recovery for exactly this symptom, no operator console needed. Post-reset verified healthy (trainer-vm-diag #6087): uptime 22m, mem 377Mi/5.8Gi used + 0B swap, ict-trainer-publish.timer active, mirror publishing again (trainer_status.json fresh, registry 80 models). NET: the swap headroom stops OOM-KILLS but does NOT stop swap-thrash-into-SSH-death — so 'the swap fix has the box stable' (resolution_criteria escape hatch) is now DISPROVEN; the subprocess-isolation refactor (keep orchestrator RSS under the 5G cap so it never pages) is the actual fix and should be done, not deferred. Interim mitigation to consider until then: a MemoryHigh throttle low enough that the orchestrator can't reach the swap-thrash regime, or a lightweight watchdog that RESETs on the banner-timeout symptom. Recurring MES/ML-lifecycle-availability risk (each wedge stalls all training until a manual/auto reset).

RESOLVED (PR #6917). (1) Subprocess-isolation premise verified ALREADY TRUE — each manifest is its own `python -m ml train` under the bash orchestrator; the dataset build / calibrators / publish are separate processes too. (2) The real residual (single-process peak RSS) fixed by load-time column projection in ml/experiments/runner.py::_load_jsonl (+ the audit subprocess) — synthetic bench 1401→271 MB @300k×40 rows (5.2×). (3) SECONDARY confirmed: dataset_builds.jsonl lives at runtime_logs/trainer/dataset_builds.jsonl (BUILD_LOG_PATH default in build_trainer_datasets.sh; verified present on-box, diag #6916). items.title: Fleet scorecard (RG3+RG4): replay pre-gate caught 2 MES heads anti-predictive live (skew); BTC 5m/15m fleet healthy + promotion-candidate; BTC 1h degrades live; MES live rows largely unlabeled
items.description: RESULTS (RG3 offline AUC -> RG4 live AUC): ALL 17 heads pass RG3 (TRUSTWORTHY_SIGNAL, AUC 0.58-0.92) -- offline discrimination is NOT the differentiator. RG4 (live-row re-score) is what separates them: (A) KEEP / promotion-ready -- BTC 5m/15m fleet holds on live rows with market features present (mf=True) and near-complete labeling (unlab 0-6): btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 0.92->0.82, btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 0.89->0.79, btc-regime-5m-baseline-v1 0.82->0.73, btc-regime-15m-lgbm-yz-v1 0.83->0.76, btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 0.81->0.72, btc-regime-15m-baseline-v1 0.75->0.69; plus mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 0.80->0.77 and mes-regime-5m-baseline-v1 0.68->0.75 (both on thin labeled samples ~200-254 of ~3000). (B) WATCH -- BTC 1h fleet degrades materially live: btc-regime-1h-lgbm-v2 0.78->0.61, btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1 0.79->0.60, btc-regime-1h-lgbm-funding-svble-v1 0.78->0.55 (AT the 0.55 floor). Clears the floor but the live edge is thin; not promotion-ready until the 1h>5m/15m degradation is understood. (C) FIX-SKEW / KILL -- the gate's catch: mes-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 0.89 offline -> 0.32 live ANTI_PREDICTIVE (the btc-regime-yz failure mode exactly; ~77 labeled rows), and mes-regime-15m-baseline-v1 0.58 -> 0.44 ANTI_PREDICTIVE (weak offline AND inverts live). (D) UNSCOREABLE on live (0 labeled live rows -> RG4 can't judge): mes-regime-1d-lgbm-v2 (242 rows), mes-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 (1629 rows), eth-regime-1h-lgbm-v1 (84 rows, too new), eth-regime-1h-lgbm-xasset-v1 (320 rows, the D2a cross-asset probe, too new). CROSS-CUTTING FINDINGS: (1) MES live rows are largely UNLABELED (unlab 1025-2777 of ~1100-3000) vs BTC unlab~=0 -> a labeling-pipeline gap specific to MES that blinds RG4 on half the fleet. (2) Two btc yz heads (5m, 1h) carry advisory-stage records with mf=False scoring 0.5 NO_EDGE -> a handful of advisory-stage logged rows lack the market-feature block (data-capture parity smell). (3) Offline AUC (RG3) green-lights all 17 incl. the 0.89->0.32 skew head -> confirms the build-time funnel must gate on RG4 (live-row parity + net-of-cost edge), not RG3 AUC.

items.title: Regime-head promotion is structurally blocked on the live_agreement gate (trade-win AUC on ~11 trades) — decide: re-target it to RG4 regime-discrimination, or wait for BTC real-money flow
items.description: GATE-CHECK RESULT: the two strongest heads — btc-regime-15m-lgbm-yz-v1 and btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 — clear EVERY gate (oos_edge +0.276/+0.265 over the modal baseline on 5 purged WF-CV folds; shadow_soak 22-31d; drift clean KS 0.16-0.17; cross_run_stability std ~0.002-0.004; non_degenerate via the imbalance-aware path) EXCEPT live_agreement (0.267 / 0.500 vs the 0.55 floor). btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 additionally fails drift (KS 0.262); btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 is too freshly retrained (1.6d soak, 1 run). The two baselines (5m/15m) correctly fail (oos_edge 0.0 + degenerate F1 0). THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM: live_agreement = rank-AUC(regime-volatility score vs realized trade WIN), measured on just 11 live BTC closed trades. (1) It is MIS-TARGETED for a regime head — a volatility-regime classifier predicts the regime, not trade outcomes; the regime-appropriate live signal is the RG4 live regime-discrimination AUC (0.72-0.76 for these two heads, strong). (2) It is SAMPLE-STARVED + structurally un-satisfiable while BTC real-money flow is thin (bybit_2 pinned near min-qty) — the SAME blocker that demoted the first advisory head (MB-20260623-001). DECISION FOR THE OPERATOR (Tier-3, gate-profile / policy): (A) re-target the regime profile's live-track-record gate from live_agreement (trade-outcome) to an RG4-style live regime-discrimination AUC (keeping all other gates) — the regime profile already drops beats_baseline on the same logic; or (B) keep the gate as-is and accept regime heads may never promote until live flow grows. NO PROMOTION recommended today (none is ready; live_agreement is 'not yet measurable', not 'passed').

items.title: Optimize live per-bar regime scoring (regime_bar_scoring.py) so it can be re-enabled without pegging the live VM — currently DISABLED, which pauses the strong regime heads' per-bar track-record accrual (blocks MB-20260529-001 / yz-1h soak)
items.description: Per-bar regime scoring scores every shadow-stage regime head on every closed bar per (symbol, timeframe). On the small live VM that pegs CPU to 95-100% and (with no cgroup isolation) starves the trader's main loop → the 2026-06-09 wedge. Same cost CLASS as MB-20260531-001 (sim per-bar feature reconstruction, which was root-caused to an O(n^2) feature rebuild and fixed byte-identically in sim/engine.py) — but the LIVE path (src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py + the ShadowPredictor.predict per head) is unoptimized. It is now DISABLED on the live VM (REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=1, observe-only so zero trading impact) — but that pauses the order-influencing per-bar track record the strong heads (1h/MES) need (MB-20260529-001), which gates the yz-1h shadow->advisory promotion evidence (MB-20260527-004). OPTIONS to evaluate: (a) batch/cache the per-bar feature build instead of rebuilding per bar+head (mirror the MB-20260531-001 sim fix); (b) limit per-bar scoring to ONLY the strong heads being promoted (e.g. btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1) rather than every shadow regime head; (c) coarsen the cadence (score the 1h head on 1h closes only, not every tick); (d) cgroup CPUWeight/nice the trader above the scoring + other sidecars (defense-in-depth, helps regardless). Then re-enable via set-env REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=0 and re-run the CPU A/B to confirm it stays bounded.
items.trigger_condition: Next /ml-review; or before re-enabling REGIME_BAR_SCORING on the live VM; or any session touching regime_bar_scoring.py / the yz-1h promotion (MB-20260527-004).
items.resolution_criteria: regime_bar_scoring.py runs on the live VM with CPU staying bounded (no sustained >~50% attributable to scoring, verified via the new status_check.sh CPU snapshot / a re-run A/B) AND the strong regime heads resume accruing per-bar shadow records — so MB-20260529-001 / the yz-1h soak are unblocked. OR a decision that per-bar scoring stays off and the regime-head track record is sourced differently.
evidence_log: 2026-06-09 (fix shipped + deployed + verified, PR #3082): SHIPPED option (a) [batch/cache per (symbol, timeframe)] + option (c) [coarsen cadence via wall-clock fetch gate] in src/runtime/regime_bar_scoring.py. Three changes: (1) Group predictors by (symbol, timeframe) so multiple heads on the same market (e.g. btc-regime-5m-v2 + btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1) share ONE network fetch + ONE shared closes view per tick instead of fetching the same Bybit/IBKR candles per head; per-head feature_row_for_predictor still runs (each head keeps its own frozen edges/labels/vol_feature_column) but over already-fetched data. (2) Wall-clock fetch gate (_BAR_SECONDS dict + _FETCH_GATE_BUFFER_S=30s): per (symbol, timeframe), skip the fetch until bar_duration - 30s have elapsed since the last fetch — 1h head ~1×/hour instead of 60×, 5m head ~1×/5min instead of 5×. A failed fetch does NOT arm the gate so a transient exchange blip never silences a head for a full bar duration. (3) Cache exchange client per emit_regime_bar_predictions call in _live_fetch_fn so BTCUSDT 5m+15m share one Bybit client. Tier-2 ship: PR #3082 (operator-approved in chat, draft→ready, auto-merge SQUASH, branch updated to base) merged at 834f7ae; pull-and-deploy via system-action #3092 landed cleanly (HEAD 7c45cad→834f7ae, ict-trader-live.service active, boot_audit 0 open packages). Tests: 28 pass (was 14) — new TestFetchGate (6 cases: default-true, unknown-tf permissive, within-gate-false, past-gate-true, 1h gate longevity, no-arm-on-failure) + TestPredictorGrouping (2 cases: two heads same (sym,tf) → one fetch; different (sym,tf) → independent fetches); ruff clean.

2026-06-09 (CPU A/B PASS, #3097): Re-enabled via set-env REGIME_BAR_SCORING_DISABLED=0 (#3093, ict-trader-live.service restarted clean). T+15min steady-state status-check #3097 (two consecutive snapshots 35s apart): loadavg 0.96/0.40/0.66 → 1.34/0.54/0.69 (1m/5m/15m on 2-core box, well under 2.0 saturation); trader process steady at 14.5%/14.6% CPU (vs 95-100% sustained at incident, vs ~5-10% with scoring OFF — i.e. ~5-10pp marginal cost for full regime-head coverage, totally acceptable). Heartbeat fresh (1-25s old at each snapshot), shadow_predictions.jsonl actively writing (size 18,226,341 → 18,226,341 bytes, mtime crossing the snapshot window — the strong heads ARE accruing per-bar records again). All canonical services active; boot_audit clean; no wedge. The brief 1-min load tick to 1.34 between snapshots is the expected sawtooth from bar-close ticks (every (sym, tf) group hits its fetch gate at roughly the same time when a 5m bar closes, then ~270s of dedup-only ticks) — peaks ~half a core, no saturation. Resolution criteria met: bounded CPU verified; strong regime heads resume per-bar track-record accrual → MB-20260529-001 / MB-20260527-004 (yz-1h shadow→advisory soak) UNBLOCKED.

Clean three-way ablation on the IDENTICAL 354-trade real-BTC live_holdout (majority baseline acc 0.7514, base rate 0.2486; joint dataset 22,814 rows = same composition as S8). joint+yz: acc 0.7203 / precision 0.2105 / recall 0.0455 / f1 0.0748 / brier 0.2185. joint-only (xsym-v1): acc 0.7571 / precision 0.5417 / recall 0.1477 / f1 0.2321 / brier 0.2201. items.source: Operator asked for a sweep ETA; profiling the running sim sweep (PID 604328) on the trainer VM surfaced an ML-inference cost concern.
items.title: Regime-gate model scoring in sim is ~0.5s/bar — ~100-1000x slower than raw LGBM inference; profile + optimize the per-bar scoring path
items.description: MEASURED, NOT ESTIMATED. The operator's sim sweep (2 variants over 60,000 BTC 5m bars: 5m_roster [no models] + 5m_gate66 [regime-gate model in loop]) ran 9.8h wall / 9.7h CPU at 98.8% CPU sustained (genuinely computing, not stuck) and had completed 0/2 variant outputs (sim writes only at the end). Decomposition: variant-1 (7 strategies, no ML) is ~12 min by local profiling (sim.engine run_replay measured at ~1.66 ms/bar/strategy on the 3.5-day sample); the remaining ~9.5h is variant-2's regime-gate scoring => ~0.57 SECONDS per bar. A trained LGBM regime classifier should infer in microseconds, so the per-bar cost is ~100-1000x what inference itself needs. Ruled out one obvious cause: the model is NOT reloaded per bar (sim/models.py ModelScorer._ensure_loaded guards with self._loaded, loads once). So the cost is in the PER-BAR FEATURE RECONSTRUCTION or the ShadowPredictor scoring wrapper, not the tree inference. Impact: any full-history sweep with a model in the loop is a 10+ hour single-core job, which (a) makes the consolidated sim harness impractical for routine model-in-loop sweeps and (b) is the bottleneck blocking the prem-tier-core work queued this session. NOT yet root-caused — needs a py-spy/cProfile pass on the actual VM scoring path (py-spy is not installed on the trainer; install or use cProfile via a wrapped run). Likely fixes once profiled: vectorize/batch the feature build across bars instead of rebuilding per-bar, precompute regime scores once per bar and reuse across variants, or cache the feature frame. This is ml-pipeline efficiency (sim scoring path), hence ml-review not health-review.
items.trigger_condition: Any /ml-review run; or any session running a model-in-loop sim sweep that takes hours.
items.resolution_criteria: The per-bar regime-gate scoring cost in sim is profiled (py-spy/cProfile on the real path) and the hot spot identified; either an optimization lands that brings a 60k-bar model-in-loop variant under ~30 min on one core, or the finding is documented as inherent with a recommended workflow (e.g. precompute-scores-once) in the sim/ docs.
evidence_log: 2026-05-31 (/health-review): VM pull on sweep PID 604328 — etime=35328s, cpu_ticks=3490149 (cpu=9.69h), bars_total=60000, variants=2, done_outputs=0. Local sim profile: run_replay no-model = 1.66 ms/bar/strategy (3000-bar sample, warmup 300). Implied variant-2 ML cost ~0.57s/bar. ModelScorer loads once (not a per-bar reload).

2026-05-31 (continuation session, LOCAL empirical profile — not the VM): built a representative regime model (200 rounds x 2 classes = 400 trees, num_leaves 31, mirroring btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2) and profiled the exact sim per-decision hot path (feature_row_for_predictor + ShadowPredictor.predict) over 60k-bar growing history. RESULT OVERTURNS THE LEADING HYPOTHESIS: single-row Booster.predict = ~79 us/call (~4.8s/60k), NOT 0.5s/bar — so 'batch the single-row predict' (the continuation prompt's 'highest-leverage unblock') would save the LEAST (batched is 42x faster per row but the smallest absolute term). Two real per-decision costs measured: (1) the engine:308 closes-rebuild [float(c) for c in history['close'].tolist()] = ~103s/60k, an O(n^2) rebuild that was ~19x pure waste (.tolist() already yields Python floats, so the float() pass re-converted them) — FIXED this session: precompute the close column once + per-bar O(1) slice, byte-identical, Tier-1 sim-only (sim/engine.py); 68 sim tests pass incl. a new byte-equivalence + no-future-leak guard in tests/test_sim_phase2.py. (2) statistics.pstdev inside rolling_log_return_vol uses exact-Fraction arithmetic (math.gcd/Fraction.__new__ dominate its cProfile) = ~13s/60k, second-largest term — a plain float/np stdev would be ~20x faster but would BREAK the #2485 byte-identicality and touches the LIVE path (Tier-2), so logged-not-slammed (follow-up: prove bucket_for_vol stability under the ~1e-15 delta before changing). CRITICAL HONEST CAVEAT: summed, these per-decision terms are ~2 min locally (~6 min at VM-core scale) — the SAME scale as #2485, so they do NOT account for the 9.5h variant-1->variant-2 delta. Ruled out locally: sim/sweep.py builds ONE ModelScorer per variant and _ensure_loaded guards the booster parse (no per-decision re-instantiation/re-parse); the model factor incl. the regime-gate 0.0 does NOT change open_position/bar-skipping (sim/engine.py:347), so decision COUNT should match across variants. Separately found a LATENT O(n^2) in the SHARED path: sim/engine.py:275 future=[df.iloc[j].to_dict() for j in range(i+1,n)] materializes ALL remaining bars as dicts per decision at ~52 us/bar (a single early decision builds ~60k future bars ~= 3s), but it is bounded by variant-1's 12 min (sparse decisions) so it is a latent landmine, NOT the 9.5h cause. NEXT (still needs the VM, per resolution_criteria): cProfile/py-spy the ACTUAL variant-2 run with the real variant configs+model+candles; prime remaining suspect is a decision-COUNT divergence between the real variant configs (does 5m_gate66 trade far more than 5m_roster?), since the per-call scoring cost is now measured-cheap.

2026-05-31 (continuation session, ROOT-CAUSED on the VM via cProfile — definitive): drove the trainer VM through the diag relay (core confirmed idle, sweep PID 604328 gone), authored a 2-variant repro (5m_roster vs 5m_gate66 w/ btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 regime_gate) over market_raw/BTCUSDT/5m/v002, and cProfiled it. RESULTS: 5m_roster 67.77s/1800-bars (37.6ms/bar, 594 trades); 5m_gate66 168.3s (93.5ms/bar cProfile-inflated, 594 trades). FIRST KEY FINDING: BOTH variants have IDENTICAL trade count (594) — the decision-COUNT-divergence hypothesis is WRONG; the gate adds only ~1.3-1.5x, not 47x. SECOND, DEFINITIVE FINDING: cProfile cumulative attributes 111.75s of 168s (66%) to sim/engine.py's `future = [df.iloc[j].to_dict() for j in range(i+1,n)]` list comp — the very line my LOCAL pass mis-filed as 'a latent landmine, NOT the 9.5h cause'. It IS the cause: it is O(n^2) (rebuilds ALL remaining bars every decision) AND each row access is pathological under pandas>=3.0 because df columns are PyArrow-backed (the profile shows pandas _ixs/fast_xs/to_dict + arrow array.__iter__ at 4.9M calls dominating). My 2000-bar slice only shows it at ~half the runtime; at the full 60k bars the O(n^2) explodes to the ~9.5h. The DB-init flood (1062 'Database tables created/verified' prints from vwap.py:685 constructing a full Database() per order_package eval) is real noise/wiring-smell but does NOT appear in the top-22 cumulative — it is NOT the bottleneck. FIX SHIPPED (Tier-1, sim-only, byte-identical): precompute all row-dicts ONCE (`all_rows = [df.iloc[j].to_dict() for j in range(n)]`) then index/slice per decision (bar=all_rows[i], future=all_rows[i+1:]) — each row deboxed exactly once, O(n) instead of O(n^2)-with-arrow-debox. 68 sim tests pass; ruff clean. CONFIRMED ON THE VM (same repro, engine patched in place then restored clean): N=2000 5m_roster 67.77s->23.89s (2.84x), 5m_gate66 168.3s->55.35s (3.04x), BOTH still 594 trades (byte-identical); the future listcomp dropped out of the cProfile top entirely (remaining cost is now strategy indicator recompute — turtle_soup._detect_setup, fade_breakout_4h._adx — a separate, smaller O(n^2)). The 2000-bar speedup understates the full-history win: future-build is O(n^2), so at 60k bars it was the dominant term (the ~9.5h), now ~linear. FOLLOW-UP (separate, Tier-2/3): vwap.py self-suppression check builds a write-capable Database() (full DDL + a stray print) per evaluation against the production journal copy — should use a lightweight read-only path and Database.__init__ should not print; logged for an operator-gated fix.

2026-06-01 (/ml-review): Closing: the root-caused sim/engine.py future-bar O(n^2) arrow-debox fix was already VM-confirmed (5m_roster 67.8s->23.9s, 5m_gate66 168.3s->55.4s, both byte-identical 594 trades) per the prior evidence entry. Resolution criteria (hot spot profiled + optimization landed) satisfied; marking resolved.

items.source: /ml-review 2026-05-27 — re-verification of BL-20260525-004 (MES regime models collapse to one class).
items.title: Experiment: forward-vol-aware vol feature for MES regime classifiers — backward vol_bucket doesn't separate forward-vol regime label on MES
items.description: After today's cycle: mes-regime-5m macro_f1=0.345, mes-regime-15m macro_f1=0.329 (both flat across 11 runs). The RegimeClassifierTrainer (ml/trainers/regime_classifier.py) is a per-bucket modal-class classifier keyed on the BACKWARD-LOOKING vol_bucket; on MES that backward vol_bucket does not separate the (forward-vol-based) regime_label, so every bucket is range-majority and argmax always picks 'range' (f1_volatile=0). BTC works because BTC vol is autocorrelated; MES intraday isn't. Three concrete experiment paths to try, in order of cheapness: (1) more vol buckets (5+ instead of 2-3) so the trainer can carve out sub-regimes that DO separate forward vol; (2) probability-threshold eval instead of argmax — surface the model's volatile-class probability and tune a threshold over the eval split; (3) a stronger continuous vol feature (e.g. realized-vol-of-realized-vol, or a forward-vol-AWARE feature like the prior bar's range expansion rate). Operator decision 2026-05-25: leave manifests as-is until a dedicated model-training session — this is that session's queue.

items.title: Decision: setup-quality-lgbm-v2 (mae 0.071 vs baseline mae 0.048 at n=76) — hold for n>=1000 or demote
items.description: setup-quality-lgbm-v2 trained cleanly (PR #2053's LightGBM stack works end-to-end) but loses to setup-quality-baseline-v0 on the same n=76 eval: MAE 0.0710 vs 0.0478, MSE 0.0114 vs 0.0092. Cause is dataset size, not model quality — 76 closed trades is too small for a gradient-boosted tree to beat a simple per-group-mean baseline. The model is currently target_deployment_stage=shadow + auto-wired into the shadow factory (default-flip 2026-05-19), so it logs predictions on every live signal. That's fine for data collection but means it shouldn't be considered for shadow->advisory promotion until either (a) on a fresh cycle with n_eval >= ~1000 it beats baseline on MAE+MSE, OR (b) it's explicitly demoted to research_only via `python -m ml promote-stage setup-quality-lgbm-v2 --new-stage research_only` (semantic change to the registry, operator-approved). This is the ml-review-backlog mirror of BL-20260526-003 (health-review backlog) — same model, recorded here so /ml-review picks it up on each run.
items.trigger_condition: Each /ml-review run; revisit specifically when n_trades >= ~1000 closed trades suitable for setup_labels, OR a dedicated model-training session reviews the v2 setup-quality manifest.

items.title: Deeper MES history: run the IBKR historical pull ON the live VM (shares the one IB gateway) and sync to trainer; resolve the Error 162 session conflict
items.description: MES regime models currently train on a rolling ~60-day ES=F 5m window from yfinance — the deepest intraday history yfinance serves and the only source reachable from the trainer VM. IBKR would give multi-year 1m MES history, but the architecture blocks it: (1) IB Gateway is a loopback-only socket on the LIVE VM (127.0.0.1:4002 via the gnzsnz socat relay) — the trainer VM cannot reach it. (2) IBKR permits exactly ONE logged-in session per username, so we can't run a second gateway on the trainer without disconnecting the live MES trader. The ibkr_offvm adapter (ml/datasets/adapters/ibkr_offvm.py) is therefore designed to run ON the live VM (guard ICT_IB_HISTORICAL_OK=1), sharing the live gateway on a DISTINCT clientId, paced gently (~12s between chunked reqHistoricalData calls), then the resulting market_raw shards sync to the trainer. (3) Current blocker: run_serious_baseline.sh's MES leg is gated behind MES_IBKR=1 (default 0) and was disabled 2026-05-22 because the gateway returned IBKR Error 162 'session connected from a different IP'. The 2026-05-28 IB-gateway auto-heal watchdog (ict-ib-gateway-watchdog) mitigates the overnight reset-wedge but does not address the historical-pull session conflict. PROPOSED PATH (Tier-2/3, live-VM, operator-gated): add a paced, low-priority IBKR historical-pull job on the LIVE VM (distinct clientId e.g. 450, useRTH=false, pause_s>=12) that writes market_raw/MES/{5m,15m,1m}/v002 and is picked up by the trainer sync; verify it does not perturb the live trading clientId; resolve why Error 162 fires (likely clientId collision or the gateway only accepting one source IP). Until then the ~60d yfinance window is the working fallback and the MES LightGBM models train on it.

items.resolution_criteria: market_raw/MES/{5m,15m} at v002 carries multi-year (or at least multi-month) IBKR-sourced bars synced to the trainer, built without disconnecting or degrading the live MES trading session; mes-regime models retrain on it. OR operator decides the ~60d yfinance window is sufficient and this is closed as won't-do.

items.source: S-MLOPT-S13 — building the per-bar regime scoring path surfaced that live regime scoring is computed under a far smaller feature set than the heads train on.
items.title: Regime-head train/serve feature parity (Phase 4.2): live scoring computes vol_bucket + one close-to-close vol value; heads train on range-vol estimators + log-return lags + time features — and the yz heads' frozen vol_feature_column (yang_zhang_vol) is computed live as close-to-close vol
items.description: src/runtime/regime_shadow.feature_row_for_predictor builds the live regime feature row as base_row + {feature_column: vol_bucket, vol_feature_column: rolling_log_return_vol value}. But the lgbm-v2 / yz regime heads' feature_columns are ~11: vol_bucket, rolling_log_return_vol, parkinson_vol, garman_klass_vol, rogers_satchell_vol, yang_zhang_vol, log_return, log_return_lag_1, log_return_lag_2, hour_of_day, dayofweek. All but vol_bucket + the single vol value are ABSENT live → LightGBM imputes NaN (handled natively, but the served vector differs from the trained one). Worse for the S9 yz heads: their frozen vol_feature_column is yang_zhang_vol, yet the live path computes plain close-to-close rolling_log_return_vol and labels it as that column AND buckets it against yang-zhang-derived edges → the live vol_bucket itself can be wrong for the yz heads. This is PRE-EXISTING (the signal-time path + the v2 heads have the same gap); S13 deliberately reused the same computation so per-bar == signal-time. FIX (Phase 4.2 train/serve parity): in the live scoring path compute (a) the range-vol estimator named by vol_feature_column from OHLC (reuse ml/datasets/volatility_estimators.py — the S9 module), and (b) the log-return lags + hour_of_day/dayofweek, so the served feature vector matches training. IMPACT: until this lands, the per-bar shadow track record S13 generates for the regime heads (incl. the yz heads we want to promote) is computed under-featured, so it must NOT be the sole basis for a shadow→advisory promotion.
items.trigger_condition: Before promoting any regime head shadow→advisory on shadow-prediction evidence; or when Phase 4.2 (train/serve parity) is taken up; or next /ml-review.
items.resolution_criteria: The live regime feature row (regime_shadow + regime_bar_scoring) computes the same feature set the head trained on — at minimum the vol estimator named by vol_feature_column (range-vol via volatility_estimators.py) plus the log-return-lag + time features — verified by a parity test comparing a live-computed row to the training builder's row for the same bar; OR it is documented + accepted that regime heads are scored on vol_bucket only and their manifests are reduced to that feature set.
evidence_log: 2026-06-06 (/ml-review): RESOLVED — feature parity confirmed DEPLOYED + live. Live shadow_predictions tail (#2868, 04:58->05:36Z 6/6) shows btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 records whose feature_row carries the FULL market_features superset (rolling_log_return_vol + parkinson_vol + garman_klass_vol + rogers_satchell_vol + yang_zhang_vol + log_return + log_return_lag_1/2 + hour_of_day + dayofweek + vol_bucket), not the old vol_bucket-only row. The S17 fix is in the running trader (sha 5fbee10). The yz heads now accrue a parity-correct shadow track record; promotion reads use post-deploy records. Closed.

2026-06-04 (S-MLOPT-S17): FIX SHIPPED (draft PR, Tier-2, observe-only). src/runtime/regime_shadow.feature_row_for_predictor now emits the full market_features superset (rolling_log_return_vol + parkinson/garman_klass/rogers_satchell/yang_zhang_vol + log_return + log_return_lag_1/2 + hour_of_day/dayofweek) computed live from the trailing vol_window_n OHLC window (new ohlc_from_candles + range_vol_estimators reusing ml/datasets/volatility_estimators.py + log_return_series + _latest_bar_hour_dow), and buckets vol_bucket against the value of the estimator NAMED BY the head's frozen vol_feature_column — so the v2 heads bucket rolling_log_return_vol and the yz heads bucket yang_zhang_vol (the core bug: close-to-close vol bucketed against yz-unit edges). Both callers (_emit_shadow_preds signal-time + regime_bar_scoring per-bar) pass candles_df= so per-bar == signal-time; a close-only fallback preserves legacy/test callers. RESOLUTION CRITERION MET: parity test (tests/runtime/test_regime_shadow_parity.py) uses MarketFeaturesBuilder itself as the oracle — the live row == the builder's row bit-for-bit (rel 1e-9) for the continuous features + a test proving the yz-bucket fix. 176 tests pass; ruff clean. CAVEATS: (1) status=resolved_pending_deploy — the track record accrued BEFORE the S17 deploy is still under-featured; promotion reads must use the record accrued AFTER pull-and-deploy. (2) The yz vol_bucket is an approximation by construction (the frozen yz edges are the per-bucket max of yang_zhang_vol where the bucket was defined by rolling_log_return_vol quantiles → monotonic-ish, not exact); the v2 heads are exact. NEXT: re-deploy, let the parity-correct record accrue, then /ml-review the strong heads (btc-regime-1h, mes-regime-1d) for a shadow->advisory promotion proposal (Tier-3, operator-gated).

items.source: Operator 2026-05-30: 'are the journal-decision models also trained on backtest results? can we backtest strategies to create more data for those models?'
items.title: Augment the journal-backed decision models (setup_quality, trade_outcomes) with PER-TRADE backtest rows to break the n~78 data wall
items.description:
STATE TODAY: the journal-backed families explicitly EXCLUDE backtests. ml/datasets/families/setup_labels.py + trade_outcomes.py source trade_journal.db::trades filtered to CLOSED + non-backtest + non-null pnl (setup_labels also requires non-empty setup_type). The only backtest family, backtest_results.py, reads the AGGREGATE backtest_results table (run-level win_rate/sharpe/total_pnl) — NOT per-trade labeled setups. So today these models train ONLY on the bot's live trades (~78), which is exactly why setup-quality-lgbm-v2 loses to its per-group-mean baseline (MB-20260527-003). FEASIBILITY: YES for setup_quality + trade_outcomes (both predict win/R from setup features available at signal time) — a 5y backtest over each strategy yields thousands of labeled setups vs 78 live. NOT for execution_quality (it learns real slippage/fills that backtests don't model — synthetic fills would poison it). REQUIRED WORK: (1) have the backtest harnesses (scripts/backtest_*.py + src/backtest) emit PER-TRADE rows in the setup_labels/trade_outcomes schema (entry/SL/TP/outcome/r_multiple + the same signal-time features), not just aggregate metrics; (2) persist them tagged source=backtest; (3) extend the families with a source column + a builder flag to include backtest rows; (4) TRAIN on live+backtest but EVALUATE on a real-trade holdout ONLY, so metrics reflect live generalization not backtest fill artifacts; (5) keep leakage discipline (features at signal time only). CAVEAT to document: backtest outcomes depend on fill assumptions (TP/SL touch, no slippage/funding/partial fills), so the augmented signal is 'would this setup hit TP before SL under idealized fills' — directionally useful, tag it. PAIRS WITH: the new 5y BTC window (PR #2399) and the FVG-strategy backtesting work — every strategy backtest becomes training data.

[VERDICT 2026-08-04] Augmentation RAN + measured (trainer #8460): a real but sub-volume edge; the wall is the TRUSTED EVAL BOOK (324 real trades), not train volume. Redirect: the lever is growing the real/paper eval book (M30/L3), NOT more train augmentation. Guard debt is now a measured, evidence-backed DEFERRAL, not neglect. See docs/research/S-P0-LABEL-AUGMENT-2026-08-04.md.

OR operator decides synthetic augmentation isn't worth the domain-shift risk and closes won't-do.

items.source: /ml-review 2026-06-01 — fresh cycle metrics showed the 5y-window widening (#2399) degraded all three btc-regime-*-lgbm-v2 models run-over-run.
items.title: BTC regime lgbm-v2 models DEGRADED on the 5y window (#2399) — sweep the training-window length / recency weighting to recover f1_volatile
items.description: After #2399 widened the BTCUSDT training window to a rolling 5 years, all three btc-regime-*-lgbm-v2 models lost headline metric run-over-run even as n_eval ~doubled: 5m macro_f1 0.546->0.524 / f1_volatile 0.107->0.070 (n 50626->105173); 15m 0.568->0.511 / 0.226->0.144 (n 16872->35054); 1h 0.633->0.609 / 0.483->0.444 (n 4214->8760). The extra (older) history appears to dilute the recent volatility regime the models had been separating — a classic stationarity/regime-shift tradeoff. This directly weakens the 6/2 shadow->advisory soak candidate (btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2, MB-20260527-004), whose volatile-class f1 is now ~0.07. EXPERIMENT: sweep the train-window length (e.g. 1y / 2y / 3y / 5y) and/or add recency weighting (sample_weight decaying with age, or LightGBM's time-decay) on the btc-regime manifests, evaluating on a FIXED recent holdout, to find the window that maximizes f1_volatile on recent data. If a shorter/recency-weighted window restores f1_volatile, propose it as the manifest default before promoting any regime model past shadow.
items.trigger_condition: Next /ml-review; or any model-training session with capacity to sweep the btc-regime training window.
items.resolution_criteria: A window/recency-weighting sweep identifies a configuration whose btc-regime-{5m,15m,1h}-lgbm-v2 f1_volatile on a fixed recent holdout beats the current 5y-window numbers; OR it's confirmed the 5y window is optimal and the degradation is accepted with rationale documented.
evidence_log: 2026-06-06 (/ml-review): RESOLVED — the recency-decay config adopted via merged #2679 (sample_weight 1h=90d/15m=60d/5m=60d) has materialised in the registry. Sweep found the per-model winners and they shipped; the experiment is complete. (Note: the live 5m head's f1_vol stays structurally low ~0.07-0.11 on the imbalanced 5m regime, but that's the regime base-rate, not the window — the recency sweep recovered what was recoverable. Further 5m gains now come from features (S9 yz already shipped) not window.) Closed; the shadow->advisory promotion is the separate operator-gated step.

2026-06-03 (/ml-review): re-confirmed, FLAT day-over-day (same 5y window, +1 day data) and now the gating experiment for the 5m soak (MB-20260527-004). 6/3 cycle (run 20260603T0035xxZ): btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 macro_f1=0.5242/f1_vol=0.0692 (n=105173); 15m 0.5106/0.1439 (n=35054); 1h 0.6096/0.4466 (n=8760). All match 6/1 within noise — the 5y window's dilution of the recent volatility regime persists. The 5m volatile-f1 sitting at ~0.07 is the single biggest reason the 5m shadow->advisory promotion is held. The window/recency sweep (1y/2y/3y/5y + age-decay sample_weight, evaluated on a fixed recent holdout) is the concrete next step to recover f1_volatile before any promotion. Notably the 1h head (f1_vol 0.447) held up far better on the wide window than 5m/15m — recency dilution hits the shorter timeframes hardest.

2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S2): window/recency sweep RUN (trainer-vm #2677, scripts/ml/window_recency_sweep.py vs a fixed recent purged holdout). CONFIRMED the dilution: f1_volatile falls monotonically with window length, 5y worst in all three models (1h 0.451->0.446 @1y->5y; 15m 0.202->0.143; 5m 0.101->0.069). RECENCY DECAY (5y+half_life=180d) recovers it: 1h 0.4601 = OUTRIGHT BEST (> 1y 0.451, > plain 5y 0.446) AND best macro_f1, keeping full 5y data; 15m 0.1916 and 5m 0.0963 recover ~80% of the 5y->1y gap at 4-5x the data (1y still narrowly best on f1_volatile for 15m/5m). PROPOSAL (Tier-3, operator-gated): adopt sample_weight half_life=180 on btc-regime-1h-lgbm-v2 (clear win); for 15m/5m run a half-life sweep (60/90/180d) before choosing window-vs-decay. Tooling: PR #2676.

2026-06-03 (regime recency follow-up): half-life sweep (#2678, hl=60/90/180/365d at 5y vs 1y baseline) gave a DECISIVE winner per model — a recency-decayed 5y window now beats BOTH the plain 5y AND the 1y window on f1_volatile for all three: 1h hl=90d f1_vol 0.4666 (vs 0.4510 @1y / 0.4455 @5y); 15m hl=60d 0.2129 (vs 0.2023 / 0.1433); 5m hl=60d 0.1154 (vs 0.1005 / 0.0692). 180d (the first guess) was too slow a decay; 60-90d is the sweet spot. Tier-3 DRAFT PR opened adopting sample_weight (1h=90d, 15m=60d, 5m=60d) on the three btc-regime-*-lgbm-v2 manifests — pending operator approval before merge. Closes the experiment; the manifest edit is the remaining (operator-gated) step.

2026-06-03 (wrap-up): Tier-3 PR #2679 MERGED (operator-approved) — sample_weight now on all three btc-regime-*-lgbm-v2 manifests (1h=90d, 15m=60d, 5m=60d). evidence_log: 2026-06-07 (S-MLOPT-S15a, trainer-vm-diag #2925/#2926): TREND-MODEL CLASS-WEIGHT TUNING + ADX HEAD-TO-HEAD DONE. On the v7 market_features 1h dataset (43,800 rows; trend label dist chop 39% / trending 34% / transitional 27%): the leak-free purged-WF-CV ADX-14 baseline (trailing ADX → forward trend label) scores macro_f1 0.3167 (chop f1 0.336 / trans 0.221 / trend 0.393). The UNTUNED LGBM trend head only ties it (0.3243) and starves transitional (recall 0.124, f1 0.167). A 6-point class-weight sweep found mild inverse-freq weights {chop:1.0, transitional:1.45, trending:1.14} are the sweet spot: transitional f1 0.167→0.276 (recall →0.286) WITHOUT collapsing chop → macro_f1 0.3403 (chop 0.393 / trans 0.276 / trend 0.353), which CLEARS ADX-14 by +0.0236 and beats it on 2 of 3 classes (chop + transitional; ADX still wins trending). Heavier weights (≥2×) over-correct (chop collapses, macro_f1 < baseline). Weights baked into ml/configs/btc-regime-1h-trend-lgbm-v1.yaml (stays research_only). VERDICT: a viable, modestly-better-than-ADX trend-axis detector candidate — honest modest win, NOT a strong one (both ~0.32 macro_f1 on a hard 3-class forward-regime problem). Remaining gates to wiring it as the live phase-4 detector (replacing ADX): a shadow track record + backtest/shadow-PnL justification (not macro_f1 alone) — Tier-3, operator-gated. items.title: Re-run setup-quality baselines under purged WF-CV before any promotion read; confirm whether setup-quality-lgbm-v2 still beats its mean baseline honestly
items.description: Under leak-free 5-fold purged WF-CV, setup-quality-lgbm-v2 scored MAE=0.086 / MSE=0.0175 vs its optimistic 80/20 holdout MAE=0.065 / MSE=0.0094 (399 rows, setup_labels all v002). The manifest notes the per-setup-mean baseline (setup-quality-baseline-v0) at holdout MAE=0.058 — i.e. under honest CV the v2 LGBM may NOT clear its own baseline. The baseline was not re-run under the same WF-CV folds, so this is not yet apples-to-apples. Also: btc-regime-1h-lgbm-v2 weighted_f1 fell 0.7185->0.6742 under WF-CV (smaller, expected optimism gap). Tool: scripts/ml/eval_split_compare.py. Feeds Phase 0.1 (now done) → relates to G4 + Phase 1 meta-labeling in optimization-roadmap.md.

Apples-to-apples re-eval of BOTH manifests via scripts/ml/eval_split_compare.py on the same 5-fold purged WF-CV (n=203 eval rows). setup-quality-baseline-v0 (per-setup-mean): purged MAE 0.07150 / MSE 0.01535; setup-quality-lgbm-v2: purged MAE 0.08249 / MSE 0.01683. **lgbm-v2 LOSES to its own per-group-mean baseline under leak-free CV** (MAE +0.011, ~15% worse). items.title: Meta-label model loses to baseline on the REAL holdout — close the synthetic↔real domain gap (wire logged signals as the setup_candidates event source)
items.description: S-MLOPT-S6 built the de-Prado meta-label model + the leak-free live_holdout eval (train on synthetic setup_candidates, score on REAL trades). Trainer-VM eval (#2697): on 352 real BTCUSDT closed trades (win rate 0.244) the model scored accuracy 0.670 vs the majority-class baseline 0.756 — it does NOT beat the baseline, so no promotion was proposed. Root cause is a large domain gap: the synthetic CUSUM/triple-barrier candidates have a ~0.457 win rate vs the strategies' real 0.244 — CUSUM momentum events are a different (easier) population than the actual setups. Highest-leverage fix: add a SIGNAL-LOG event source to ml/datasets/families/setup_candidates.py (sample candidate events from trade_journal.db::signals / signal_audit.jsonl at the strategies' real decision points) so the train distribution matches real setups, then re-run the live_holdout eval. Compose with S7 (backtest-augmented real labels, enlarges the real holdout) and S8 (cross-symbol). The live_holdout machinery makes each measurable.
evidence_log: 2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S6 trainer-VM #2697): build BTCUSDT setup_candidates (15732 synthetic) + REAL-trade holdout from data/trade_journal.db (352 BTCUSDT closed, win_rate 0.244); meta-label (LightGBMRegressionTrainer->won, ClassificationEvaluator, live_holdout) scored acc=0.670 prec=0.266 recall=0.198 f1=0.227 brier=0.219 on the 352 real trades; majority-class baseline acc=0.756. Model < baseline => not promotable. Synthetic win rate ~0.457 vs real 0.244 = domain gap.

2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S6 follow-up, this session): the Tier-1 enabler landed — ml/datasets/families/setup_candidates.py now accepts signal_log_db=<trade_journal.db>; every side=buy|sell row in trade_journal.db::signals (the audit-log dual-write — strategies' real decision points) is located at the bar covering its logged_at_utc and labeled with the SAME triple-barrier as CUSUM. New row tag event_source ∈ {cusum,signal_log,live} disambiguates the three samplers. Backwards-compatible include_synthetic retained; new include_cusum is the preferred name. New manifest ml/configs/setup-candidates-metalabel-siglog-v1.yaml (Tier-3 proposal, research_only) mirrors S6 (live_holdout, LightGBMRegressionTrainer->won) but trains on the signal-log distribution. 8 new unit tests added; full tests/ml/test_setup_candidates.py + cross_symbol + metalabel + splitters = 51 passed; ruff clean.

2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S6-FU trainer-VM eval #2716): built v003 dataset (signal_log train rows=8739 win=0.469; live eval rows=352 win=0.244; include_cusum=false), trained the meta-label, eval on the same 352 real BTCUSDT holdout. **Signal-log meta-label**: acc=0.526 prec=0.290 recall=0.651 f1=0.401 brier=0.417. **Majority-class baseline**: acc=0.756. **Signal-log model < baseline; ACCURACY WORSE than the S6 CUSUM run (0.526 < 0.670) — not promotable**. Honest read: signal-log win rate (0.469) is almost identical to CUSUM (0.457), so the 'CUSUM is easier than real setups' hypothesis was wrong — both synthetic populations are equally pulled from a different distribution than real trades (0.244). The recall jumped (0.198 → 0.651) because the train base rate is higher, biasing the predictor upward; precision barely moved (0.266 → 0.290); brier doubled (0.219 → 0.417). **Real root cause: triple-barrier on synthetic candles uses optimistic fills + no real slippage + no real risk-manager filtering; the strategies' actual trades lose more because real execution + real risk gating filter the obvious winners OUT, leaving structurally harder cases.** No amount of 'better train-event-sampling' closes this gap — the LABELS are the wrong distribution. Next lever: backtest-augmented labels with REAL fill modeling from the standalone harnesses (scripts/backtest_squeeze.py / backtest_fade.py / backtest_trend.py / backtest_ict_scalp.py / run_backtest_vwap.py), via S-MLOPT-S7 backtest_recorder ported to setup_candidates — that's the apples-to-apples distribution. The enabler + manifest stand as Tier-1 infrastructure (useful for future event-source mixing); the manifest stays research_only.

2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S6-FU-2, this session): backtest-label event source landed as the next lever. setup_candidates.py now accepts backtest_trades_db=<db> (+ include_backtest convenience reusing live_trades_db, + backtest_strategies filter): every is_backtest=1 row (recorded by ml.datasets.backtest_recorder from the standalone strategy harnesses) is located at its entry bar and emitted tagged event_source='backtest' + is_live_trade=False, carrying the harness's ACTUAL realized outcome (won from the recorded R-proxy pnl), NOT a synthetic triple-barrier. New manifest ml/configs/setup-candidates-metalabel-backtest-v1.yaml (Tier-3, research_only) mirrors the S6/S6-FU live_holdout protocol but trains on the backtest distribution. 8 new tests; full tests/ml/test_setup_candidates.py+metalabel+splitters=55 passed; ruff clean; end-to-end build validated (leakage passed, backtest train + live eval partition). Tracking the headline trainer-VM eval under MB-20260603-003.

items.title: Backtest-labeled setup_candidates: re-run the live_holdout meta-label eval with backtest-train + real-eval (the apples-to-apples distribution the signal-log run approximated)
items.description: S-MLOPT-S6 (CUSUM, acc 0.670) and S-MLOPT-S6-FU (signal-log, acc 0.526) both lost to the majority baseline (0.756) on the 352 real BTCUSDT holdout. The signal-log eval (#2716) ruled out the EVENT SAMPLER as the lever — swapping CUSUM momentum events for the strategies' real decision points barely moved the synthetic train win rate (0.457 -> 0.469). The remaining suspect is the synthetic triple-barrier LABEL (optimistic fills, no slippage, no risk gating). S-MLOPT-S6-FU-2 ports the S7 backtest_recorder pattern to setup_candidates: the strategies' standalone harnesses (scripts/backtest_{squeeze,fade,trend,ict_scalp}.py, src/backtest/run_backtest_vwap.py) already model real slippage + actual entry/exit logic, so each backtest trade is a real-distribution label at a real signal time. Tier-1 enabler (backtest_trades_db source, event_source='backtest') + Tier-3 manifest (setup-candidates-metalabel-backtest-v1, research_only) shipped this session; the headline trainer-VM eval (build backtest-train + real-eval -> train -> score the 352 real holdout vs baseline) is the open step.
evidence_log: 2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S6-FU-2 enabler): ml/datasets/families/setup_candidates.py — added _load_backtest_trades (is_backtest=1 reader, optional strategy filter) + backtest_trades_db / include_backtest / backtest_strategies kwargs; backtest rows tagged event_source='backtest', barrier_touched='backtest', is_live_trade=False (train side of live_holdout), won from the recorded R-proxy pnl, r_multiple=pnl. Manifest setup-candidates-metalabel-backtest-v1.yaml (research_only) mirrors S6/S6-FU. 8 new tests + full suite 55 passed; ruff clean; end-to-end build leakage_test_status=passed.

2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S6-FU-2 trainer-VM eval #2718): built BTCUSDT setup_candidates v001 backtest-train + real-eval (include_cusum=false): 2,653 backtest rows (squeeze 963 + fade 1690, recorded is_backtest=1 from the standalone harnesses via scripts/ml/record_harness_trades) + 352 real BTCUSDT eval rows (win 0.244, majority baseline 0.756). Trained setup-candidates-metalabel-backtest-v1 under live_holdout, scored on the 352 real holdout: **accuracy 0.756, precision 0.50, recall 0.047, f1 0.085, brier 0.196.** Read: this is the BEST of the three label sources (acc 0.756 vs CUSUM 0.670 vs signal-log 0.526 — backtest labels closed most of the synthetic<->real gap) AND the best calibration (brier 0.196 vs 0.219/0.417), with **precision 0.50 lifting off the 0.244 base rate** (a real, if low-volume, signal). BUT accuracy only TIES the majority baseline (0.756) — recall 0.047 means the model essentially predicts the majority class (loss) for almost all rows, so accuracy ≈ baseline by abstention. NOT a promotion-worthy beat. **Eval is incomplete:** (1) backtest_ict_scalp.py lacks an --emit-trades flag (only --json summary) so ict_scalp was excluded — adding the flag is a Tier-1 follow-up; (2) squeeze+fade ran on the 1h market_raw base (timeframe approximation — both are 4h strategies; fade was deeply net-negative across years on 1h, likely poor-quality trades). Recommend a cleaner re-run (add --emit-trades to ict_scalp + run harnesses at native timeframes) before any further call. Manifest stays research_only; promotion past shadow operator-gated.

2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S6-FU-2 cleaner re-run #2723/#2724, detached): all THREE BTC harnesses at native timeframes — ict_scalp 5m (60k-bar window, 128 trades) + squeeze 4h (226) + fade 4h (439) = 793 is_backtest=1 train rows + 352 real eval rows (win 0.244, baseline 0.756). TRAIN: accuracy 0.741, precision 0.40, recall 0.116, f1 0.180, brier 0.199. **Slightly WORSE than the 1h run (#2718: acc 0.756, prec 0.50) — does NOT beat baseline (0.741 < 0.756).** The cleaner native-TF set has far fewer rows (793 vs 2653; 4h squeeze/fade produce 1/4 the trades of 1h), and the smaller/cleaner distribution didn't help. CONCLUSION across all 4 label sources (CUSUM acc 0.670 / signal-log 0.526 / backtest-1h 0.756 / backtest-native 0.741): backtest labels are the BEST source by PRECISION (0.40-0.50 > the 0.244 base rate — a real, consistent signal that real-execution labels are closer to the real distribution), but NONE beats the majority baseline on accuracy at n=352 — the model abstains (low recall) because the real holdout is 75.6% losses. This is a DATA-SCALE FLOOR at n~352, exactly as the roadmap predicted. The lever to break it is more real data (time) or better features (S-MLOPT-S9, which DID show a positive regime f1_volatile lift), not another label distribution. The backtest-label infrastructure (event source + recorder bridge + ict_scalp --emit-trades) stands as reusable tooling; the manifest stays research_only.
items.resolution_criteria: The backtest-labeled meta-label, re-evaluated on the REAL-trade live_holdout, beats the majority-class baseline on accuracy AND shows positive precision lift over the 0.244 base rate (=> propose Tier-3 promotion past research_only) — OR the negative persists across all three label sources (CUSUM, signal-log, backtest) and is documented as a data-scale floor at n~352, pivoting to better features (S-MLOPT-S9 range-based vol estimators / Phase 2).

2026-06-03 (S-MLOPT-S9 A/B #2720): rebuilt market_features BTCUSDT 1h v002 on builder_version v3 (range-vol columns confirmed present), trained champion vs challenger under the manifest time_aware_holdout. **Champion btc-regime-1h-lgbm-v2 (close-to-close vol): f1_volatile 0.4624, accuracy 0.744, macro_f1 0.647, weighted_f1 0.771, precision_volatile 0.355, recall_volatile 0.661.** **Challenger btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1 (range-based vol, spec frozen on yang_zhang_vol): f1_volatile 0.4724, accuracy 0.760, macro_f1 0.659, weighted_f1 0.783, precision_volatile 0.372, recall_volatile 0.646.** **POSITIVE: every metric improved — f1_volatile +0.010, accuracy +0.016, macro_f1 +0.011, weighted_f1 +0.012, precision_volatile +0.017 (recall_volatile -0.015, a precision/recall trade favoring precision).** Modest but consistent lift; the range-based vol features genuinely help regime separation. CAVEAT: this is the time_aware_holdout (same split for both heads, so the delta is fair) NOT the Phase-0 purged WF-CV — a purged-CV confirmation is the rigorous follow-up before promotion.

2026-06-04 (S-MLOPT-S9 finish, purged-CV confirm #2736): rebuilt market_features BTCUSDT 1h/5m/15m on builder_version v4 and ran scripts/ml/eval_split_compare.py (5-fold purged & embargoed WF-CV, label_horizon=5, embargo_fraction=0.01) on BOTH the v2 champion AND the yz challenger, identical folds. **1h purged WF-CV: yz beats v2 leak-free on EVERY headline metric — f1_volatile 0.5036 vs 0.5009 (+0.0027), macro_f1 0.6609 vs 0.6542 (+0.0067), accuracy 0.7372 vs 0.7258 (+0.0114).** (Same run's holdout: yz f1_volatile 0.4694 vs 0.4655, +0.0039 — same sign, so the holdout lift was not an artifact; both heads' purged-CV f1_volatile ~0.50 > holdout ~0.47 because the recent-20% holdout is the harder block.) The S9 range-vol lift HOLDS under the rigorous leak-free CV. **PROMOTION PROPOSAL (Tier-3, operator-gated, NOT flipped):** advance btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1 research_only -> shadow as the new 1h regime champion candidate (clean leak-free improvement over the current shadow champion). NOTE: full shadow->advisory is separately blocked by MB-20260529-001 (1h regime heads emit zero shadow predictions until the S13 per-bar scoring path). 5m/15m BTC + 5m/15m MES yz A/B manifests shipped (research_only); their purged-CV A/B results + the MES build are appended here as the trainer jobs (#2736 BTC 5m/15m; a follow-up MES job) complete — only positive leak-free heads are proposed for shadow.

2026-06-04 (S-MLOPT-S9 BTC 5m/15m purged-CV A/B #2736 complete): **ALL THREE BTC timeframes POSITIVE on f1_volatile under the Phase-0 purged WF-CV (leak-free), largest lift at the shorter TFs where the volatile class is rarest:** 1h yz 0.5036 vs v2 0.5009 (+0.0027); 5m yz 0.1535 vs v2 0.1362 (+0.0173); 15m yz 0.2532 vs v2 0.2316 (+0.0216). macro_f1 + accuracy also up on all three (5m macro +0.0092/acc +0.0025; 15m macro +0.0149/acc +0.0144). The range-based vol feature genuinely improves volatile-regime separation across the whole BTC regime stack. Promotion proposal extends to 5m/15m: advance btc-regime-{1h,5m,15m}-lgbm-yz-v1 research_only->shadow (Tier-3, operator-gated). MES 5m/15m yz A/B (needs median-calibrated MES market_features rebuild) + the S11 funding A/B are the remaining trainer jobs.

2026-06-04 (S-MLOPT-S9 MES A/B #2745, median-calibrated build): MES yz is MIXED, NOT a clean win. MES 5m: yz f1_volatile 0.7305 vs v2 0.7261 (+0.0044) BUT macro_f1 0.5329 vs 0.5507 (-0.0178); MES 15m: yz f1_volatile 0.7108 vs v2 0.6889 (+0.0219) BUT macro_f1 0.5294 vs 0.5573 (-0.0279). accuracy up on both (5m +0.0155, 15m +0.0093). Read: on MES the regime classes are MEDIAN-CALIBRATED (~balanced ~50/50), so the range-vol feature shifts the precision/recall tradeoff TOWARD the volatile class (f1_volatile up) at the EXPENSE of the range class — macro_f1 (which weights both classes equally) drops. Contrast BTC, which is heavily range-imbalanced (~80-99.5% range), where the same feature lifts f1_volatile with NO macro cost (macro up on all 3 BTC TFs). So range-vol is a CLEAN win on the imbalanced BTC regime heads (proposed research_only->shadow for btc-regime-{1h,5m,15m}-lgbm-yz-v1) but INCONCLUSIVE on the balanced MES heads — NOT proposed for MES promotion (the macro_f1 regression is the blocker; if the operator only cares about volatile-class recall the MES yz heads are arguably better, but on the balanced metric they're worse). Honest mixed result; the MES yz manifests stay research_only as documented A/B candidates.

items.title: Crypto funding-rate + open-interest features: A/B the funding-augmented regime head vs the v2 champion (quantify the f1_volatile lift)
items.description: S-MLOPT-S11 (M14 Phase 2.3) added the cheapest unused crypto-perp feature family: Bybit funding-rate z-score/extremes + open-interest change, joined into market_features (builder_version v3->v4) as five past-only, as-of-aligned columns (funding_rate / funding_rate_zscore / funding_rate_abs_z / open_interest_change / open_interest_change_zscore) behind an optional funding_oi_path. Research nuance baked in: funding is a TRAILING byproduct of momentum so the signal is in the z-score/|z| EXTREMES, not the level; OI is fed as a change, not a non-stationary level. New manifest btc-regime-1h-lgbm-funding-v1.yaml (research_only) is a clean A/B vs btc-regime-1h-lgbm-v2 (identical trainer/split/weighting; only the funding/OI columns added). The open step is the trainer-VM A/B: (1) fetch the funding/OI side-stream (ICT_OFFVM_BUILD_HOST=1 python -m scripts.ml.fetch_funding_oi --symbol BTCUSDT --start <s> --end <e> --oi-interval 1h --out datasets-out/funding_oi/BTCUSDT/v001), (2) rebuild market_features 1h v4 with funding_oi_path joined, (3) run scripts/ml/eval_split_compare.py on both manifests under the Phase-0 purged WF-CV and read the f1_volatile delta. Attacks gap G5 (no funding/OI features). The build-script opt-in is ICT_BUILD_FUNDING_OI=1.

Tests: test_funding_oi_features.py + test_bybit_funding_oi.py + market_features funding additions; ruff clean; local stdlib smoke (columns present + non-zero with a side-stream, all-zero without, emitted keys == schema, as-of alignment past-only). A/B eval pending the funding-joined v4 rebuild on the trainer VM.

2026-06-04 (S-MLOPT-S11 funding A/B #2745, trainer VM): the off-VM Bybit V5 funding/OI adapter WORKS end-to-end on the trainer (fetch_funding_oi: funding_rows=5460 = full 5y 8h coverage; open_interest_rows=191 = ONLY ~8 days — Bybit's public OI history retention is short). Rebuilt 1h market_features v4 with the funding/OI join; sanity-checked v2 on the funding-joined dataset = f1_vol 0.5009 (identical to the no-funding build → v2 correctly ignores the funding columns). **A/B (purged WF-CV, leak-free) NEGATIVE: btc-regime-1h-lgbm-funding-v1 f1_volatile 0.4859 vs v2 0.5009 (-0.0150), macro_f1 0.6513 vs 0.6542 (-0.0029), accuracy 0.7328 vs 0.7258 (+0.0070).** Funding/OI did NOT improve the 1h regime head's volatile separation. HONEST READ: (1) OI coverage was ~8 days only (retention), so the open_interest_change/zscore columns are ~all-zero across the dataset — effectively only the funding-rate features (z-score/|z|, full coverage) were tested; (2) those added slight noise the booster overfit (f1_vol down 0.015). The research nuance held in spirit — funding's level is a trailing momentum byproduct — but the extracted extreme features did not separate the *volatility* regime label better. No promotion proposed. The S11 infra (estimators + off-VM adapter + as-of join + fetch CLI + opt-in build wiring) stands as reusable, leakage-safe tooling; manifest stays research_only. Follow-up levers (not pursued this session): wire funding/OI into setup_candidates (a momentum/positioning target may suit it better than the vol-regime label); a deeper OI source (Bybit retention limits the public history — a rolling forward capture would accrue it); or a different funding_window. The OI-retention finding is the key blocker for the OI half.

items.title: Order-flow / VPIN features: build the Tier-2 live L2 capture path, then A/B OFI/VPIN/microprice vs the regime champions
items.description: S-MLOPT-S10 (M14 Phase 2.2) shipped the Tier-1 estimator core (ml/datasets/orderflow_features.py: Cont OFI, Easley-LdP-O'Hara VPIN + bulk-volume classification, Stoikov micro-price, relative spread; CI-tested). UNLIKE S9 (range-vol from OHLC) and S11 (funding/OI from REST history), order-flow needs L1/L2 + trade-tick data we do NOT capture and CANNOT backfill (no public L2 history endpoint), so it cannot be A/B'd offline — S10 is a two-part sprint and the Tier-2 live-capture path is the gate. Design proposal in docs/ml/orderflow-capture-design.md: store PER-BAR aggregates (ofi/vpin/rel_spread_mean/microprice_dev) as a market_microstructure side-stream (mirrors the S11 funding/OI as-of-join + drift machinery, storage-bounded), joined into market_features via an optional microstructure_path (builder_version v4->v5). THREE OPERATOR DECISIONS needed before building: (1) capture host — trainer-VM side-car (preferred, WS9-safe) vs dedicated tiny OCI host vs (rejected) live-VM; (2) transport — free REST polling on Bybit (recommended start) vs paid ccxt.pro WebSocket; (3) scope — BTCUSDT-only to start (recommended) vs also MES/IBKR depth (needs a paid subscription, shares the live IB session). On sign-off: build the capture service (Tier-2) -> accrue >= a few weeks -> build the join columns + A/B manifest (Tier-1/3) -> purged-CV A/B vs the v2/yz champions. Microstructure alpha decays — monitor via KS/PSI drift if promoted.

items.title: Macro/cross-asset A/B for MES: eval mes-regime-5m-lgbm-macro-v1 vs mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 once MES market_features rebuilds on v6 with a macro side-stream
items.description: S-MLOPT-S12 (M14 Phase 2.4) shipped the cross-asset/macro feature group for MES: ml/datasets/macro_features.py (VIX level/z + term-structure slope VIX/VIX3M-1, DXY z+return, 10y level + 3m-10y slope), the off-VM yfinance_macro fetch adapter + scripts/ml/fetch_macro.py, market_features builder_version v5->v6 (optional macro_path, default-preserving 0.0), and the research_only manifest ml/configs/mes-regime-5m-lgbm-macro-v1.yaml (identical to v2 except the added macro group; same frozen regime spec). The daily build_trainer_datasets.sh fetches the macro stream once (ensure_mes_macro, MES_MACRO=1 default-on, NON-FATAL) and joins it into the 5m/15m + 1d MES market_features via macro_path. ACTION when the next daily cycle has rebuilt MES market_features on v6 WITH the macro stream present (check the build emit for family=macro status=ok + the v002 MES feature dir carries non-zero vix_level): run `python -m ml compare mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 mes-regime-5m-lgbm-macro-v1` and read the f1_volatile delta under the Phase-0 purged CV. If macro separates the MES volatile regime where same-OHLC vol did not -> propose promotion to shadow (operator-gated). If not -> HONEST NEGATIVE: log it here and move on (intraday macro alpha is plausibly thin; MES is daily-conditioned at best). Leakage discipline already enforced: daily features are one-day-lagged (a day-D row stamped D+1) + as-of past-only joined (unit-tested).
evidence_log: 2026-06-14 (model-training, MES pull-fix session) — CLOSED NEGATIVE. Ran the formal `python -m ml compare mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 mes-regime-5m-lgbm-macro-v1` on FRESH NATIVE MES history. Backstory: the pull tool (scripts/ops/pull_mes_ibkr_history.sh) had been silently broken since the 2026-06-10 gateway-isolation — it still defaulted IB_HOST=127.0.0.1 (the retired same-box loopback), so every MES pull died in ~2s with ConnectionRefused. Fixed in #3500 (default -> 10.0.0.251, the dedicated gateway VM), deployed, re-ran: MES 5m=17,113 rows / 15m=5,717 (~1y native intraday). Cycle head=65a3b6e4 rebuilt MES market_features ON the native data (build emit 'using synced IBKR MES market_raw'). RESULT (holdout n_eval=3418, 20% of 17k): f1_volatile v2=0.623 vs macro-v1=0.459 (delta -0.164); recall_volatile collapsed 0.694->0.387; weighted_f1 0.686->0.637; precision flat (~0.565). items.description: S-MLOPT-S12 Part B (roadmap Session 2.4 second deliverable: 'wire the existing-but-unused account_context family -- equity curve / daily PnL / open-trade count -- into the decision models') was scoped but NOT shipped this sprint, for two honest blockers. (1) NO MANIFEST consumes ml/datasets/families/account_context.py today (it produces the was_taken label + mission-rule features but is an orphan family). (2) The equity-curve / daily-PnL / open-trade-count the roadmap wants are NOT recorded as AS-OF-SIGNAL-TIME snapshots: trade_journal.db::daily_risk_state (src/units/accounts/risk.py) stores only end-of-interval daily running values (daily_pnl, daily_high_equity, current_equity), so deriving a signal-time feature post-hoc would LEAK -- the stored daily_pnl includes PnL from trades AFTER the signal. Also the prop accounts account_context targets are sparse/dry, so a manifest today may be untrainable. TWO SUB-OPTIONS: (a) MINIMAL safe wire -- once prop-account was_taken volume is confirmed non-trivial (verify via an /ml-review diag pull of trade_journal.db::trades WHERE account prop + status in {open,closed,rejected}), add a research_only manifest training on the EXISTING leakage-safe columns (mission rules + skip_reason excluded as a leak per the family docstring). (b) PROPER enrichment -- instrument per-signal account-context snapshots (equity, daily-PnL-so-far summed only over trades closed strictly before the signal ts, open-trade count) at decision time, persist them, then join. (b) is the real value but is live-path-adjacent (Tier-2 instrumentation). Recommend (a) gated on the data check, then (b) if (a) shows signal.

INVESTIGATION (operator chose hold+investigate over demote). ROOT CAUSE FOUND via live shadow_predictions feature_row (diag #4511). (1) PARITY IS WIRED, not the bug: feature_row_for_predictor (S-MLOPT-S17) populates yang_zhang_vol + all 4 range estimators + lags + time features live (both per-bar AND signal-time callers pass candles_df); the live values are real (e.g. btc-1h yang_zhang_vol=0.006493), NOT NaN. The regime_bar_scoring.py module-header 'Feature-parity caveat' (lines 65-73, claiming the estimators are absent live -> NaN and 'must land before shadow->advisory') is STALE doc-drift, contradicted by both the code and the live data. (2) THE REAL BUG = yz vol_bucket edge miscalibration: on the SAME bar, the yz heads bucket vol systematically LOWER than their v2/baseline siblings. btc-1h @ yang_zhang_vol=0.006493 -> v2/funding heads bucket vol_b2 (score 0.56), yz head buckets vol_b0 (score 0.92); btc-15m @ 0.00207 -> baseline/v2 vol_b1, yz vol_b0. The yz heads' frozen vol_bucket_edges (computed on yang_zhang_vol at train time) don't match the live yang_zhang_vol scale, so live vol almost always lands in the lowest bucket b0 -> the model's most important categorical feature is near-constant -> the BTC yz heads saturate (~0.92-0.98) -> degenerate. (Note: the broad btc-regime saturation [baseline+v2+yz all ~0.97-0.99 on 5m/15m] is ALSO partly market-driven — BTC is in a persistent low-vol range — which inflates the stage-guard drift-vs-train metric; regime-confidence != trade-outcome, so the auc/brier-vs-trades attribution is a partial category mismatch. But the yz-specific b0 lock is a genuine calibration defect distinct from that.) FIX (Tier-3, retrain): re-freeze the yz heads' vol_bucket_edges against the live-consistent yang_zhang_vol distribution (verify the estimator's train-vs-live window/annualization parity first), then re-gate before any re-promotion. SEPARATE Tier-1 doc fix: correct the stale regime_bar_scoring.py header caveat (parity landed in S17). Demote remains the safe interim (operator holding); the degenerate yz advisory keeps feeding c_reg a near-constant value meanwhile.

RE-GATE RESULT (operator-approved re-freeze retrain, trainer #4519, python -m ml train --no-register so the SERVED advisory was untouched). Fresh re-frozen vol_bucket_edges: 5m [0.003040, 0.003877] (macro_f1 0.559, f1_volatile 0.125); 1h [0.007615, 0.019984] (macro_f1 0.665, f1_volatile 0.487). DECISIVE: the re-freeze does NOT clear the b0 lock — current live yang_zhang_vol (5m ~0.00156, 1h ~0.006493 from diag #4511) is STILL below the freshly-recomputed b0->b1 edge on BOTH heads (5m 0.00156<0.00304; 1h 0.006493<0.007615) => both still bucket vol_b0. So the degeneracy is NOT a stale-model artifact: BTC's CURRENT low-vol regime sits below the bottom bucket of even a fresh (60d-recency-weighted) edge set, so a simple retrain can't salvage the yz advisory. RECOMMENDATION FLIPS to DEMOTE now (evidence-backed): demote btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1 advisory->shadow. Re-promotion would need a DEEPER Tier-3 redesign — shorter edge-freeze recency window, finer low-end bucket granularity, or moving off fixed-quantile bucketing — validated before any promote. The 1h head is borderline (0.006493 vs 0.007615) so it'd flip to b1 on a small vol uptick, but is also b0-locked right now.

NEW MECHANISM (RG2 replay-pregate session, 2026-06-25 ~22:20Z) — the advisory degeneracy has a SECOND, distinct root cause this item missed, on a DIFFERENT scoring path than the vol_bucket-edge issue (which was diagnosed on the SHADOW path). Evidence: live /api/bot/shadow/stats for btc-regime-1h-lgbm-yz-v1 (#4596) shows TWO record sets — `shadow` stage: row_keys_seen = FULL market_features (yang_zhang_vol, vol_bucket, rolling_log_return_vol, log_return, hour_of_day...), score spread 0.50-0.99 (the enriched per-bar path #4511 examined); `advisory` stage (count 183, 06-13->06-23 = the exact promote->demote window from stage_history #4601): row_keys_seen = ONLY {confidence, direction, killzone, setup_type, strategy_name, symbol} — ZERO vol features — and score 0.977-0.989, a degenerate CONSTANT. ROOT CAUSE: src/runtime/advisory_sizing.py::compute_advisory_factor scores every advisory predictor on _feature_row_from_pkg(pkg) (6 bare OrderPackage fields, designed for the trade-outcome models) and does NOT call feature_row_for_predictor to enrich — unlike the signal path (_emit_shadow_preds, which enriches-or-skips) and the per-bar path (regime_bar_scoring). So a regime head at advisory is scored on a row with ALL its market_features missing -> LightGBM emits a near-constant ~0.98 -> that constant is what the stage-guard auc-0.40 / brier_lift -0.277 attribution actually measured (NOT the edge-bucketing). IMPLICATION: edge re-calibration alone (the prior conclusion) CANNOT make advisory promotion of ANY regime head work — even a perfectly-calibrated head gets a bare row at advisory and saturates. FIX (Tier-3, order-influence path) — two options for the operator: (A) enrich in compute_advisory_factor via feature_row_for_predictor (needs candles for the pkg symbol/tf at sizing time; skip/score-None a regime head that can't be enriched rather than log a constant) — mirrors _emit_shadow_preds; OR (B, cleaner) EXCLUDE regime heads from the advisory directional-downsize quorum entirely — a regime P(volatile) score is not a bullish/bearish directional view, so feeding it into the 'bearish quorum' downsize is a category error regardless of enrichment; regime conviction belongs in the c_reg lens, not the downsize quorum. RECOMMEND (B) + a promotion-gate guard that refuses to promote a predictor to advisory until its advisory-path score distribution is verified non-degenerate. Surfaced as a Tier-3 proposal on PR #4602. This is the load-bearing reason BOTH yz advisories (1h MB-20260623-001 + 5m here) went degenerate the moment they were promoted.

Confirmed coverage: BTC fresh 06-26, ETH 06-17, MES 06-12 (coverage probe scripts/ml/_labeling_gap_probe.py). FIX (commit 7a051e5): generalized build_btcusdt_pair -> build_bybit_pair(symbol,tf) + added ETHUSDT/1h + SOLUSDT/1h to the daily loop (same market_features params as BTC; the eth head is 'identical to btc-regime-1h-lgbm-v2 except the symbol'). KEY FINDING: the now-scoreable ETH heads are NO_EDGE on live rows -- eth-regime-1h-lgbm-v1 RG4 0.46 (111 labeled), eth-regime-1h-lgbm-xasset-v1 RG4 0.46 (347 labeled) -- vs RG3-offline 0.70-0.73. That is TRAIN/SERVE SKEW (offline/clean-candle good, live logged-rows ~random), the same class as the BTC yz heads. CONSEQUENCE: the ETH multi-symbol-A backtest A/B ($63->$2336) is optimistic for LIVE -- it scored the head on clean harness candles; live the head feeds a ~random vol label. ETH is NOT live-ready. RG4 prevented a bad promotion. NEXT: (1) retrain the ETH regime head / investigate the offline-vs-live feature parity (why it discriminates offline but not on logged live rows) until it clears RG4 (>=0.55 live); (2) MES 5m (RG4 0.765) is the actually-promotable alt; (3) SOL head training. The fix is durable: any alt head is now RG4-validatable each cycle.

CLASS-WEIGHT RECALIBRATION shipped (PR #8345). New root-cause LAYER complementary to the 2026-06-28 feature-skew finding, not a replacement: eth-regime-15m-lgbm-v1 ports BTC's class_weight volatile:28 verbatim, which is ~1/base-rate for BTC's 4.46% 15m volatile rate — but ETH's realized rate at the frozen vol_threshold=0.005 is 9.22% (~2x BTC's; measured on the exact training dataset, trainer-diag #8341). So 28x over-weighted the minority class ~2.6x -> the booster over-commits to volatile, which COMPOUNDS the live feature-distribution shift already noted (live rolling_log_return_vol +51% vs train). In-session --no-register A/B on ETH v002 (trainer-diag #8342): f1_volatile 0.278@28x -> 0.313@15x -> 0.331@11x -> 0.338@8x, monotonic, as precision_volatile rebalances 0.171->0.252 (recall 0.754->0.517). Recalibrated to 11x (=1/0.0922, fleet-consistent inverse-base-rate recipe; keeps better volatile recall than 8x, which matters for a protective gate). CAVEAT (honest): this is the OFFLINE holdout calibration fix — it is the necessary precondition for a fair RG4 re-read, NOT a proven live-NO_EDGE resolution; the feature-skew half (live vol >> 5yr train mean) may remain and only a fresh RG4 soak under 11x settles it. NEXT (unchanged, post-soak): RG4 the recalibrated head at matched vol_threshold=0.005; if robustly >=0.55, re-run the ETH A/B + cell-selection WF and propose advisory promotion (Tier-3). items.source: trainer-diag #4892/#4893. RG4 (scripts/ml/replay_pregate_live.py) defaults vol_threshold=0.003, but every Bybit (symbol,tf) market_features dataset is built with vol_threshold=0.005 (build_trainer_datasets.sh::build_bybit_pair). RG4 must score a head against the SAME regime_label definition it trained on; the 0.003 default mis-scores all Bybit heads.
items.title: RG4 harness scores at vol_threshold=0.003 but Bybit heads train at 0.005 -> read the threshold from the dataset, don't hardcode
items.description: Impact measured by a threshold sweep: btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 RG4 0.79@0.003 -> 0.83@0.005; btc-1h 0.62->0.58; btc-15m 0.73->0.71; eth-regime-1h-lgbm-v1 0.46->0.58 (the 0.46 'NO_EDGE' in MB-20260627-003 was substantially this artifact, though the ETH head is still only knife-edge at 0.005 so the verdict holds). The fix: replay_pregate_live (and rg4_targeted.sh / fleet_scorecard.sh) should resolve vol_threshold from the dataset build metadata (market_features metadata.json records the build params) or the head's manifest, falling back to 0.003 only when unknown. NOTE MES uses a DATA-DRIVEN median vol_threshold, so a single hardcoded value is wrong for the fleet anyway -- metadata resolution is the correct fix. rg4_vt_sweep.sh (committed this session) is the interim workaround (pass the threshold explicitly).
