items.source: scripts/ml/_feature_parity_probe.py (trainer-diag #4869). The ETHUSDT/1h v002 market_features training dataset has xa_breadth_up = all-zeros (mean 0, std 0 over 43800 rows) -- the cross_asset side-stream was dead at build time -- while the LIVE logged rows carry real xa_breadth_up ~0.45. eth-regime-1h-lgbm-xasset-v1 therefore trained on dead peer features and is NO_EDGE live (RG4 0.46-0.51 across all thresholds).
items.title: ETH 1h cross_asset side-stream is all-zeros in the training dataset -> xasset regime head trained on dead xa_* features
items.description: The cross_asset build for the ETHUSDT/1h market_features dataset is producing a zero xa_* block (at least xa_breadth_up; likely xa_peer1/2_* too). The daily build_trainer_datasets.sh::build_bybit_pair for ETH does NOT pass a cross_asset_path, so market_features emits the xa cols as defaults/zeros while the live per-bar scorer (cross_asset_live.py, CROSS_ASSET_LIVE_DISABLED default-off) computes real peer features. That train/serve gap makes eth-regime-1h-lgbm-xasset-v1 untrustworthy. FIX: have the daily build construct the ETH cross_asset side-stream (scripts.ml.build_cross_asset --target ETH market_raw --peer BTC --peer SOL) and pass cross_asset_path to the ETH market_features build (mirroring how the head's manifest header documents it), then retrain the xasset head and RG3/RG4 it. Until fixed, the xasset variant should not be promoted; the base eth-regime-{5m,15m} heads (no xa) are the live path.

items.source: Operator approved enforcing the Design-A trend_vol OFF-cells live. Reading the code surfaced two blockers before any real-money flip: (1) REGIME_ML_VERDICT_MODE=use was a documented PLACEHOLDER (intents.py) — the gate always used the frozen vol label, never the ML label; (2) the live code resolves the advisory head by the STRATEGY timeframe (trend_donchian 1h / squeeze_breakout_4h 4h) but the validated A/B used the BTC 15m advisory head (btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2) as the single per-symbol vol label for ALL BTC cells. items.title: Design-A vol-gate go-live: use-substitution WIRED (#4896); need per-symbol vol-head resolution (15m head for BTC cells) + enforce guard before real-money flip
items.description: DONE: wired REGIME_ML_VERDICT_MODE=use to substitute the advisory head's ML vol label into the gate decision (intents._decision_vol_regime, fail-permissive -> frozen on unknown), tests + CLAUDE.md doc-fix (#4896). KEY DESIGN FINDING: the validated A/B (clock_tf=15m, ml_model_id=btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2) applied the SINGLE 15m advisory head's vol label to ALL BTC strategy cells regardless of the strategy's own timeframe -> the vol regime is a per-SYMBOL market label, not per-strategy-timeframe. So the go-live does NOT need 1h/4h advisory heads; it needs the LIVE resolver to use the symbol's advisory head (btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2, already advisory + RG4-robust 0.71-0.83) for the BTC cells. REMAINING (production plan): (A2) per-symbol vol-head resolution (resolve by symbol, not strategy timeframe); (A3) ML-only-enforce guard (only drop a vol cell when vol_label_source==ml, never enforce on a frozen fallback); (B) deploy + REGIME_ML_VERDICT_MODE=use + soak to confirm vol_label_source=ml resolves live for the 1h/4h BTC strategies; (C) REGIME_ROUTER_ENABLED=true to enforce, verify regime_hard_gate enforced:true + vol_label_source=ml. items.source: Inventory pass for docs/research/capital-allocation-ai-DESIGN.md (M18). Assessed whether the live-logged substrate is sufficient to TRAIN a cross-strategy expected-net-R ranker. Join order_packages -> trades is clean (realized_R = pnl / (|entry-sl|*qty) derivable; trades schema src/units/db/database.py:119-148), and decision-time features are rich (order_packages.model_scores database.py:228, account_context_snapshots context_snapshot.py:35-52, conviction inputs). The single biggest blocker: per-trade transaction cost is NOT separately logged. Fees/funding are modeled in backtests only (FEE_BPS_ROUNDTRIP=7.5 backtest_system.py:97; taker 0.055%/maker 0.02% backtester.py:30) and offline prop MC (swap 0.033%/day breakout.yaml); at live decision/close time the cost component is not separable in trades.pnl, and multi-day perpetual FUNDING may not be fully captured in the local-compute PnL path.
items.title: Per-trade cost capture (fee_*/funding_* on the close path) — the data gap blocking a clean net-R ranker label/feature; enables MB-20260629-ALLOC-RANKER
items.description: Add per-trade cost fields written on the close path (Tier-1, no order-flow mutation): fee_taker_usd / fee_maker_usd (broker fill fees), funding_paid_usd (cumulative perp funding), and a per-cell swap accrual for prop. Writer: execute.py / order_monitor.py close path, sourced from the broker's fill + funding records where available, else a fixed cost-model estimate flagged as approximate. WHY: realized net-R is the ranker's LABEL and cost is a discriminable FEATURE; without it labels are inflated ~10-20 bps (worse for multi-day perps) and the model can't learn 'high-fee scalp into small TP' vs 'low-fee swing'. Interim: Phases P0-P2 use a fixed cost model (round-trip taker bps from instruments.yaml + per-cell swap from the prop ruleset). This item is the Tier-1 substrate that must land in M18 P0 before the P3 learned ranker is trained on clean labels. Compose with db-wiring (new columns wired to the canonical store, no stray journal).
items.trigger_condition: M18 P0 (substrate) kickoff; or next /ml-review assessing allocator-ranker training readiness.
items.resolution_criteria: fee_*/funding_* columns added to trades + populated on the live close path (verified non-null on real closed trades across brokers that expose fees); a clean offline net-R label query (order_package -> trade -> net_R) reproducible for the ranker dataset. Honest negative acceptable if a broker cannot expose per-fill fees (record the fixed-estimate fallback + its calibration gap).
updates: 2026-07-17 (Slice A landed, #6750): the fixed-estimate cost floor is live — backfill-trade-costs system-action stamped fee_taker_usd + cost_source='estimate' on the whole historical book (712/712 uncosted rows), so a net-R label has a consistent modelled cost. fee_maker_usd / funding_paid_usd stay NULL pending broker truth.

2026-07-17 (Slice B / B0 built, branch claude/broker-truth-cost-backfill): the broker-truth PLAN is B0 join-key -> B1 funding pull -> B2 exact-join fee/funding sweep. B0 shipped this PR: the exchange-fills store (runtime_state/exchange_fills.sqlite) already carries per-fill fee + is_maker keyed by exchange_fills.order_id (Bybit orderId), and the trade's ENTRY orderId was already captured — but only inside notes.trade_id (JSON), not a first-class column. B0 promotes it to an indexed trades.broker_order_id column (_migrate_add_broker_order_id + the open-path insert now writes it + a backfill-broker-order-id system-action copies it from notes.trade_id for history), so the eventual fee sweep is an EXACT indexed join, not a fuzzy (account,symbol,side,qty,time-window) heuristic that could double-count fills across overlapping same-symbol trades. Observability-only (never read on the order path). TWO GAPS the Explore map surfaced that B0 does NOT close (operator-visible, tracked for B1/B2): (1) FUNDING has no source in the fills store (fetch_my_trades = execution list, no perp funding) -> funding_paid_usd needs a NEW Bybit /v5/account/transaction-log pull (B1); (2) broker SL/TP EXITS fill under an orderId the bot never sees (clients.py:775-778), so the entry-orderId join catches only the ENTRY leg -> the B2 sweep must attribute the exit leg by FIFO over the fills stream (each fill consumed once) rather than a naive time-window join, and netting (two strategies sharing one exchange position) makes per-strategy-trade fee split inherently approximate on a netted account. DECISION FOR OPERATOR before B2 --apply: (a) fees-now / funding-as-B1-later acceptable, or funding required in one slice; (b) exit-leg FIFO attribution method sign-off. No cost overwrite ships until that steer + a dry-run coverage report on the live book.

items.source: docs/research/capital-allocation-ai-DESIGN.md (M18) Phase 3. Today nothing ranks competing candidate trades head-to-head by expected value: conviction.py is a hand-weighted P(win) blend (observe-only), regime heads are gates not rankers, flip_ev.py is pairwise only, run_ev_montecarlo is offline per-cell. The allocator needs a learned 'expected net-R given decision-time features' model to rank the full candidate batch.
items.title: Train a cross-strategy expected-net-R ranker (LightGBM, new task family) for the portfolio allocator — rides candidate->shadow->advisory; advisory-only influence
items.description: New model family (a regressor/ranker, NOT a vol classifier — a genuinely new task vs the current regime heads). TARGET: realized net-R per order package (needs MB-20260629-ALLOC-COSTCAP for clean labels; fixed-cost-model labels for the first pass). FEATURES (already logged): confidence, model_scores {model_id:{stage,score}}, meta (setup_type/killzone/bias), conviction inputs (c_strat/c_setup/c_wr/c_reg), the per-SYMBOL advisory regime label (ml_vol_regime_for_symbol), and the account_context_snapshots row (equity, daily PnL, daily DD%, open-trades-count) keyed by (order_package_id, account_id). FEATURES TO ADD: per-symbol/per-asset-class exposure at decision time (today only a raw open_trades_count) + the correlation feature from MB-20260629-ALLOC-CORR. SAMPLE-SIZE REALITY: ~500-2000 live closed real-money trades exist — thin per-strategy; pool across strategies (strategy as a feature) + augment with backtest-labeled decisions for the first model, treat live shadow accrual as the validation stream. Manifest under ml/configs/, dataset built on the trainer VM, scored through ShadowPredictor (logs to shadow_predictions.jsonl). Output ranks the candidate batch; only influences the order package at ADVISORY stage after operator-approved promotion; rules EV (conviction-based) stays the fail-permissive fallback + the shadow baseline it must beat.
items.trigger_condition: After MB-20260629-ALLOC-COSTCAP (clean labels) + M18 P1/P2 (rules EV + greedy selector soaking); when >= ~1000 pooled labeled decisions are queryable; next /ml-review.
items.resolution_criteria: Ranker trained + at shadow, beating the rules-based EV baseline on held-out net-R (purged WF-CV, leak-free) and passing an RG-style robustness/skew check on logged-live rows; a promotion recommendation (shadow->advisory) prepared for operator approval. Honest negative recorded if it cannot beat the rules baseline (data-scale floor — keep the rules EV).

AUC gate PASSED: walk-forward pooled OOS AUC 0.611 market-only up to 0.680 with owner/cell, per-fold min >= 0.55 on every stack (no knife-edge) -- materially above the 06-30 ~0.51. BUT the sizing-normalized concurrency-capped selection backtest FAILED: the learned-ranker arm net -586 vs shared_priority -547 (learned_beats_priority_net=false, delta -39) and vs the EV scorer arm -375 (delta -211). The AUC is between-owner base-rate, not a within-tick cross-symbol selection edge; the rules EV scorer stays the selector (it DID beat priority in this window, +172). M18 P2/P3 (allocator selects the subset) stay PARKED. Full write-up: docs/research/T1.3-ranker-findings-2026-07-16.md. Track closed; reopen only with a within-tick contrastive target + clean cost labels (ALLOC-COSTCAP) + a net-positive opportunity set.

items.source: docs/research/capital-allocation-ai-DESIGN.md (M18) Phase 3 / gap #2. Nothing live computes correlation or covariance between symbols/positions: config/cross_asset.yaml peer features feed shadow regime heads only (cross_asset_live.py, observe-only) and are not a portfolio risk input. Two highly-correlated longs are sized as two independent risk_pct trades, so correlated exposure the caps never see as one.
items.title: Decision-time correlation/covariance feature — doubles as the allocator's covariance-adjusted risk-budget input and a ranker feature
items.description: Compute a rolling cross-pair correlation/covariance over the candidate set + the open book at decision time, log it (extend account_context_snapshots or a sibling table), and use it two ways: (1) as the covariance-adjusted marginal-risk term in the M18 capital allocator (discount a candidate's risk budget by its correlation to the existing/selected book, so correlated trades don't both get full budget); (2) as a feature for MB-20260629-ALLOC-RANKER (learn 'this signal fired when portfolio vol was already elevated' vs 'isolated entry'). Build once, log once, reuse. Reuse the offline cross_asset.yaml peer pure-fns where possible (live==train). Fail-permissive (a correlation error degrades to no-discount, never strands a signal).

items.source: During the 2026-06-30 /ml-review, `python -m ml stage-guard` proposed DEMOTE for the live advisory regime head btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 (advisory->shadow) with reason 'live calibration worse than base rate (brier_lift -0.16256)' computed from rank-AUC/Brier of the regime-vol SCORE vs realized trade WIN on n=15 closed trades. But Option A (PR #4700, merged 2026-06-27) already established this trade-outcome axis is MIS-TARGETED for a regime head and made live_agreement NON-BLOCKING in `gate-check`, replacing it with live_regime_discrimination (RG4). Same-session RG4 for this head reads 0.801 (advisory) TRUSTWORTHY -- it is NOT degrading on its proper axis.
items.title: stage-guard's DEMOTE path for advisory REGIME heads still uses brier_lift(score vs trade-win) -- the mis-targeted axis Option A retired from gate-check; align it to RG4 regime-discrimination
items.description: The shadow->advisory gate (ml/promotion/gates.py) was redesigned under Option A so a regime head is judged on live_regime_discrimination (RG4), not live_agreement (trade-win AUC). But the DEMOTE half of the lifecycle -- ml stage-guard's advisory-degradation trigger -- still demotes a regime head on brier_lift of the head's score vs trade WIN (an inherently mis-targeted axis: a vol-regime classifier predicts the regime, not trade outcomes; n is also tiny, 15 trades). Result: stage-guard mechanically recommends demoting a perfectly healthy advisory regime head (RG4 0.80) on a metric the promotion side already deemed invalid for regime heads. This is a false-positive demote signal that, if acted on, would strip the BTC vol-gate's order-influencing head right as the enforce decision (MB-20260627-001) matures. FIX (Tier-1 code, then the demote is sound): make stage-guard's advisory-degradation check for regime-family heads gate on RG4 live-regime-discrimination collapse (e.g. RG4 < 0.50 over a sufficient labeled sample) rather than brier_lift(score vs win); keep the trade-win/brier_lift trigger for the decision/outcome model families where it is the right axis. Until fixed, /ml-review and /system-review must NOT act on a stage-guard demote of an advisory REGIME head without an RG4 cross-check (this review did: HOLD, not demote).

items.source: M19 T0.1 vol_threshold sweep on the BTC-15m regime head (purged-CV, base features): the head is DATA-STARVED at its shipped vol_threshold=0.005 (4.6% volatile base rate) where f1_volatile is only 0.24, and becomes materially more discriminative at a lower threshold — f1_volatile 0.24 (0.005) -> 0.30 (0.004) -> 0.38 (0.003). Surfaced while characterizing where the frozen-TSFM embedding lift lives (trainer issues #5311/#5320/#5321).
items.title: BTC-15m vol-regime head is weak at its own 0.005 operating point (f1_volatile 0.24); a lower vol_threshold (~0.004) is materially more discriminative — evaluate the head's operating threshold on the RG4 axis
items.description: Independent of embeddings, the base BTC-15m regime head classifies the volatile class poorly at the vol_threshold the live vol-gate uses (0.005 -> 4.6% base rate -> f1_volatile 0.24, recall 0.51/precision 0.16). The class is so rare at 0.005 that the head can barely learn it. Dropping to 0.004 (8.4% base rate) lifts base f1_volatile to 0.30; 0.003 (11.7%) to 0.38. QUESTION FOR THE REGIME TRACK: is 0.005 the right 'volatile' definition for the gate, or should the head be trained/operated at ~0.004 where it genuinely separates the classes? A lower threshold ALSO makes the T0.1 frozen-embedding lift worthwhile (Δmacro_f1 +0.037 at 0.004 vs a marginal +0.012 at 0.005 — the embedding only helps where the class is populated). This is Tier-3 because the head's vol_threshold defines the live vol-gate's 'volatile' operating point (REGIME_ML_VERDICT_MODE=use, BTC enforce is LIVE) — evaluate + propose, do not change unilaterally.

Cross-referenced to the M19 T0.1 threshold-sensitivity evidence (docs/research/T0.1-embedding-followup-evidence-2026-07-01.md § Threshold sensitivity).
evidence_log: 2026-07-01 (trainer-vm-diag #5311/#5320/#5321, purged-CV BTC-15m, base vs base+32 tsfm_emb): vol_threshold sweep — base f1_volatile / (Δmacro_f1 from embeddings): 0.003=0.38/(+0.052), 0.004=0.30/(+0.037), 0.005[shipped]=0.24/(+0.012), 0.006=0.19/(-0.004). The head's own volatile-class quality and the embedding lift both decay monotonically with the volatile base rate; the shipped 0.005 sits in the weak/marginal zone.

2026-07-16 (POSITIVE FIRST-GATE; candidate manifest btc-regime-15m-lgbm-vt004-pcv-v1, purged 5-fold CV, n_train 175272 / n_eval 87636): a live-faithful mirror of lgbm-v2 with a denser volatile label reads f1_volatile 0.4377 / macro_f1 0.6275 / recall_volatile 0.769 / precision_volatile 0.308 vs the shipped 0.005 head's ~0.24 — thesis confirmed (0.005 is data-starved; a denser label separates the classes). CAVEAT: the vol_threshold=0.004 build produced a 14.05% volatile base rate (12314/87636), which matches the T1.1 track's 0.003 mapping (0.004→7% there), NOT 0.004 — so the specific operating threshold is NOT pinned; the build-param base-rate semantics disagree across tracks and must be reconciled. Item stays OPEN: live threshold unchanged (0.005); remaining Tier-3 gates = mapping reconcile → RG4 (scripts/ml/rg4_targeted.sh) → vol-gate backtest A/B → operator. Evidence: docs/research/MB-20260701-vt004-evidence-2026-07-16.md.

items.title: T1.1 deep-sequence (TCN) head is a CLEAN NEGATIVE vs the LightGBM regime head - price-only depth exhausted; pivot to T1.2 breadth + graduate the T0.4 fc head
items.description: RESULT: btc-regime-15m-tcn-v1-gpuburst (purged-CV): macro_f1 0.534, f1_volatile 0.162 (3.6% volatile base rate). Incumbent btc-regime-15m-lgbm-base-pcv-v003: macro_f1 0.560-0.582, f1_volatile 0.190-0.390 (on-disk metrics at 2%/14% base rates). The TCN is BELOW the tree on BOTH macro_f1 and f1_volatile against either incumbent baseline -> win bar (beat both by >0.01) met on neither -> left at candidate (inert), NOT promoted. CONCLUSION: a deep sequence model over raw bars does not beat the class-weighted boosted tree here. With T0.1 (frozen embeddings, marginal) this is the SECOND independent negative on PRICE-ONLY representation -> depth over a single instrument own bars is exhausted; the untested lever is BREADTH: T1.2 self-supervised encoder on the WIDE MULTI-ASSET CORPUS feeding the boosting heads (no labels needed). ALSO graduate the proven T0.4 fc_* head (candidate) to shadow via the mirror-publish serve job. DROP T1.1b (Transformer): TCN did not near-miss (~0.05 macro_f1 gap). CAVEAT: base rates not perfectly matched; a controlled re-run on identical market_features (vol_threshold 0.005) would tighten but not overturn the ~0.05 gap.

2026-07-06 (label-sensitivity arms, issues #5647/#5650, $0.076): the 0.005 negative is SPARSITY-CONFOUNDED. Same TCN/CV/eval-rows at denser labels: f1_volatile 0.162 (3.6% base rate, 0.005) -> 0.282 (7.0%, 0.004) -> 0.423 (14.0%, 0.003); macro_f1 0.534 -> 0.590 -> 0.635. At matched 14% prevalence the vt003 TCN reads above the LightGBM REGISTRY-row numbers (0.423/0.635 vs 0.390/0.560) but that row is a different protocol - NOT a controlled A/B. Decider: matched-label LightGBM control (market_features @ vol_threshold 0.003, identical purged CV) - cheap CPU train on the trainer, next session. Neither arm promotion-eligible (non-production label). Full write-up: docs/research/T1.1-tcn-label-sensitivity-evidence-2026-07-06.md.

2026-07-06 08:46Z (matched-label control, #5658/#5669, $0.10): VERDICT AGAINST THE TCN. LightGBM at the SAME 0.003 label / purged CV / inverse-frequency weighting reads f1_volatile 0.4441 vs the TCN's 0.4229 (TCN loses by 0.021) and macro_f1 0.6287 vs 0.6351 (TCN +0.006, inside the >0.01 noise bar). The sparsity confound is RESOLVED: density lifts both families roughly equally; the tree matches-or-beats the causal TCN at every matched operating point tested. T1.1 negative CONFIRMED, unconfounded. No further TCN arms planned. Full table: docs/research/T1.1-tcn-label-sensitivity-evidence-2026-07-06.md (VERDICT section).

items.source: M19 T1.2 P2 A/B: the self-supervised corpus encoder's corpus_emb block was A/B'd into the BTC-15m vol-regime boosting head under purged-CV across two corpus widths (13-series v005 and 28-series widened v006, #5539). items.title: T1.2 corpus-SSL embedding: task-matched-head probe (regime head is a closed negative)
items.description: The daily-panel SSL embedding fails the intraday BTC-15m vol-regime head because of a representation-target CLOCK mismatch (daily macro/rates/FX/credit backdrop vs 15-min volatility bursts). The reusable follow-up is NOT more corpus width or a bigger encoder (both fail the same way) — it is a head whose TARGET lives on the same daily/cross-asset clock as the corpus: e.g. a daily direction/risk head, or the M18 cross-sectional expected-net-R ranker over a multi-symbol daily universe (the M18 tabular ranker hit only OOS AUC ~0.51, and embeddings were the untested lever there). Only pursue if/when such a head is on the table; the corpus store + ssl_corpus_encoder + parity gate are already built and reusable.

items.title: fc→SL/TP geometry offline backtest INCONCLUSIVE: forward triple-barrier re-sim fails reality-calibration (real-realized -0.68R vs fixed-resim -0.06R, ~0.6R gap) so the fc-vol-scaled +0.42R 'edge' is an in-simulator artifact, not a real-money result.
items.description: The anchor arm exposed the confound: real-realized (ground-truth pnl/risk_$, mean_R -0.675) and fixed-resim (same SL/TP re-simulated, mean_R -0.058) diverge by ~0.6R. The forward triple-barrier engine answers a counterfactual the live system does not run ('hold to SL/TP or the 24h cap') — live trades close mostly on fees/slippage, monitor exits, flip-policy closes, and netting-guard/reconciler closes, NOT clean barrier hits. Since fc-vol-scaled uses the SAME engine, its +0.47R apparent improvement over fixed-resim is measured inside a simulator ~0.6R too optimistic vs a losing ground truth (real BTC trades lose 0.68x intended risk) — an artifact of how scaled barrier distance interacts with the max-hold mark-to-close cap, not a validated edge. fc's validated use (vol-regime classifier feature, at shadow) is unchanged; no order-path change proposed.

items.source: M19 next-direction deep-research (D2). The trade-outcome heads are an order of magnitude under any defensible sample-size standard (conviction n_eval=20/5 positives; ranker 214 labelable order-packages vs 16-32 dims; EPV literature: ~10+ events/variable as a floor and even that unreliable - Riley et al.). But the journal already holds 3,179 trades / 2,756 order-packages INCLUDING paper (diag #5613) - ~10x the ~350 real-money rows, same strategies/signal builders/feature surface. The meta-labeling literature (JFDS series, Joubert et al.; Hudson & Thames reproduction; E-mini triple-barrier study arXiv 2209.04895) validates the secondary-model-on-own-outcomes frame the conviction stacker already uses.
items.title: D2 label-wall spike A: meta-labeling trade-outcome heads on the FULL journal (real+paper pooled, account_class domain flag), real-money slice as the held evaluation
items.description: Retrain the conviction/trade-outcome heads on real+paper pooled with an account_class domain-flag feature (~2,700+ labelable rows), purged CV, EPV-disciplined feature budget (<= n_positives/10 effective dims), probability calibration per the JFDS meta-labeling calibration paper (calibration helps fixed sizing methods, not learned ones). EVALUATION: real-money rows as the decisive held slice - paper execution differs (fills/slippage/sizing), so paper-trained lift must show up on the real slice or it does not count. Triple-barrier labels over historical bars are allowed ONLY as auxiliary/pre-training signal (our own anchor result shows barrier outcomes diverge ~0.6R from live closes - MB-20260705-FC-SLTP-GEOMETRY); a promotion decision label stays a realized trade outcome. NO GAN/synthetic augmentation (memorization risk documented at n~100). Offline, Tier-1, $0 (CPU; a burst retrain would be <$1 if wanted).
items.trigger_condition: Re-run when the harness's pre-cutoff paper n_train approaches ~1x the real n_train (contemporaneous accrual), or a new paper account back-fills history.
items.resolution_criteria: Either (a) a pooled-label head clears purged-CV on the real-money slice with a defensible n -> promote-candidate + shadow-soak proposal; or (b) paper->real transfer fails on the real slice -> D2 closes until real labels accrue (account-sizing decision), recorded as an honest negative.

All three arms produce identical predictions (AUC 0.697 primary / 0.622 fold-0.3; acc = majority baseline 0.653; recall_win 0 at the 27% base rate). S-MLOPT-S6 bar NOT cleared; the S8 analogy does not transfer (S8 pooled cross-SYMBOL = contemporaneous; real-vs-paper is cross-TIME = chronologically disjoint). EPV 5-7 across arms - unpowered on feature quality regardless. Disposition: keep OPEN for re-run as contemporaneous history accrues (re-run when pre-cutoff paper n_train approaches ~1x real n_train; harness prints it). items.title: Train a dedicated EXIT head: P(recover >= X R from here) over in-trade state
items.detail: Experiment spec: build a per-bar in-trade dataset from historical closed trades (features: age_bars, open_r, mfe_so_far, mae_so_far, chop_frac_so_far, dist-to-trail in R, native-TF vol/trend features; label: whether the trade's FINAL realized R exceeds its current mark by >= +0.25R, i.e. 'holding from here paid'). scripts/research/m20_exit_analysis.py::trade_path already computes the path primitives; the label needs no simulation (pure truncation observables, same honesty as the M20 memo counterfactuals). Train LightGBM per timeframe-family; evaluate OOS AUC + a threshold sweep as an exit trigger vs the shipped hard stale-stop. Gate: only worth wiring if it beats the hard rule's delta on the same history. Second experiment: fc-range-scaled TRAIL distance (trail_mult x fc_range_rel/median) evaluated with the same harness lever pattern. items.title: btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1 (+ 5m siblings) OOMs ALONE on the 6 GB trainer -- pick a Rule-3 disposition (shrink / GPU-burst / drop)
items.description: The 5-minute BTC regime heads exceed the 5 GB MemoryMax cgroup cap on their own (not contention -- the heavy-job queue already serializes heavy jobs). The cycle now auto-quarantines a manifest after 3 consecutive OOM/timeout failures (BL-20260717-TRAINER-SINGLE-MANIFEST-OOM, src/utils/trainer_manifest_health.py) so it stops burning the 30-min window every cycle, and emits a manifest_quarantine_tripped cycle event as the durable escalation. That stops the WASTE but the manifest still needs a human disposition (Rule 3, docs/claude/trainer-resource-protocol.md): (a) shrink its peak RSS -- LightGBM is CPU-bound so chunk the dataset / shorten the 5m history window / cut feature count (preferred; a GPU won't speed a LightGBM fit); (b) run it on the GPU burst just to get it off the 6 GB box; or (c) drop/split it. Decide, apply, and the quarantine self-clears on the next successful train. Confirmed manifests: btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1 (exit 137 on 2026-07-03 + 2026-07-15; the 18.7h wedge that motivated the per-manifest timeout), plus the cascade siblings btc-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 and btc-regime-5m-lgbm-yz-v1.

items.title: TIER-3 DECISION: btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 (live BTC vol-gate advisory head) shows significant drift -> demote advisory->shadow, retrain, or hold?
items.description: Operator decision required (Tier-3, order-routing-affecting). Options: (a) DEMOTE advisory->shadow via the promote-stage CLI with --new-stage shadow (plus --by/--reason) -- FAIL-PERMISSIVE: with no advisory BTC head the gate reverts to the frozen vol_detector label (ml_vol_regime_for_symbol -> unknown -> frozen); it strands no signal, just stops using the drifted ML label. (b) RETRAIN/REPLACE: a fresh btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 run, or promote a cleaner sibling once one clears live_regime_discrimination + drift_clean (none do as of 2026-07-17). (c) HOLD + re-check the next daily report if the drift is a transient reference-window artifact. NOT actioned autonomously -- demoting/promoting a live advisory head is Tier-3. Evidence: docs/research/M25-readiness-assessment-2026-07-18.md; report runtime_logs/trainer_mirror/promotion_readiness/2026-07-17/. Related: MB-20260701-001 (vol-gate operating curve, negative), MB-20260628-VOLGATE-GOLIVE.

updates.note: REFRAMED after diagnosis (gate-check + shadow-drift, issue #6837). The demote is NOT warranted right now: the 'significant' drift that triggered the 2026-07-17 report has SELF-CORRECTED. As of 2026-07-18T08:13 gate-check drift_clean PASSES (KS 0.191 <= 0.2) and shadow-drift verdict is 'moderate' / PSI 'no_change'. The head is retrained DAILY (training_cycle manifest_ok 07-16, 07-18), and the 07-18 retrain pulled the drift back under threshold -- so drift is a transient daily-snapshot signal here, not a demote trigger. The REAL persistent problem is live_regime_discrimination: FAIL, RG4 AUC 0.530 (< 0.55) -- the live head barely beats random at separating regimes, and it STAYS there across daily retrains, so retraining the same manifest does not fix it. A dataset audit flagged dead feature(s)/degenerate label for this manifest (manifest_audit_flagged 07-16 + 07-18) -- the likely root cause; specifics being located (#6839). VERDICT: neither demote nor naive-retrain. The lever is a FEATURE/LABEL fix shipped as a NEW model version (forward research), then operator promotes the validated replacement; the daily retrain keeps drift in check meanwhile so the live head is not actively harmful. This case seeded the standing drift-remediation process: docs/runbooks/model-drift-remediation.md + .claude/skills/drift-remediation/SKILL.md (distinguish transient drift from persistent capability failure; never reflex-demote on one daily snapshot). oos_edge still uncomputed (gate-check --datasets-root drops the inline relay; run it in-cycle).

ROOT CAUSE FOUND (dataset_audit.jsonl, runtime_logs/trainer/, issue #6839): the 'vol_bucket' feature is 100% NaN -- a DEAD feature (nan_fraction 1.0, 'column absent/null/non-numeric for ~all rows', quarantined) across the BTCUSDT 15m regime manifests (btc-regime-15m-lgbm-vt005-pin-v1, -yz-v1, and v2 which shares the same market_features BTCUSDT 15m v002 dataset + feature set). vol_bucket is the PRIMARY categorical feature in btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2's manifest (feature_columns[0], categorical) -- for a volatility-regime classifier it is THE key vol signal. So the head trains with its main vol feature entirely absent, which directly explains the near-random live_regime_discrimination (AUC 0.530). The label is healthy (range 167294 / volatile 7978, 2 classes, not flagged). THIS IS A DATASET-BUILD BUG, not a model-architecture problem: vol_bucket is not being populated in the market_features 15m build. FIX (Tier-1 data-pipeline, autonomous): restore vol_bucket population in the 15m market_features dataset family builder -> rebuild -> retrain -> re-check live_regime_discrimination. If the AUC clears 0.55, the retrained version is the promotion replacement (operator Tier-3). NEXT ACTION: investigate the market_features family vol_bucket column build for the 15m timeframe (why it is null for all rows) and fix it. Runbook: docs/runbooks/model-drift-remediation.md worked example.

CORRECTION of the prior update: the 'vol_bucket dead feature = root cause' claim was WRONG. Verified against ml/datasets/audit.py: _audit_feature computes nan_fraction via _to_float() numeric coercion, so a categorical STRING column (vol_bucket = vol_b0/vol_b1/vol_b2) reads as 100% NaN even though it is fully present and healthy (the same audit row shows n_unique=3). Reproduced locally: vol_bucket -> nan_fraction 1.0 BUT n_unique 3, flagged True (false positive); a genuinely dead column -> n_unique 1. So vol_bucket is NOT dead and is NOT the cause of the poor discrimination. The real cause of live_regime_discrimination AUC 0.530 is the GENUINE fleet-wide discrimination weakness (the vol-gate operating-curve study MB-20260701-001 conclusion), with no single dead-feature smoking gun. Forward lever = genuine feature/label research (better discriminating inputs), shipped as a new version, operator-promoted only once it clears the gate. Neither demote nor a quick data-repair. SEPARATELY FIXED the underlying audit bug (BL-20260718-AUDIT-CATEGORICAL-FALSEPOS): _audit_feature now counts only truly-missing (absent/None/'') values toward nan_fraction and never flags a multi-value categorical as dead (+ a constant-categorical catch), with tests. Honesty note: I published the wrong root cause to main (PR #6840) and told the operator before verifying the audit's coercion semantics; corrected here + in the runbook worked example.

updates: 2026-07-18 diagnosis (docs/research/M25-btc-regime-robustness-diagnosis-2026-07-18.md, issue #6842): NOT a dead label -- a same-symbol/same-TF sibling btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 (forecast features + purged-CV) already PASSES live regime-discrimination at 0.614 (vs v2's 0.530) with clean drift (KS 0.072), 14.9d soak. So option (b) resolves concretely: the robust replacement exists in shadow. Forward path = mature fc-pcv (run gate-check --datasets-root for oos_edge; extend soak to >=20.9d; confirm live fc-feature parity) -> Tier-3 promote fc-pcv->advisory + demote v2->shadow. Also: drift self-corrected on v2 (KS 0.173 <= 0.2 PASS on the 2026-07-18 retrain) so a demote-for-drift is NOT warranted; the real issue is live discrimination, not drift. yz-v1 ruled OUT (live AUC 0.463 below random). Do NOT demote v2 meanwhile -- fail-permissive, not actively harmful, daily retrain keeps drift clean.

CORRECTION of my own 07:45 escalation note, which was based on stale backlog data. A live gate-check dispatched this session (issue #7299) shows the swap ALREADY EXECUTED: btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v1 is now at current_stage='advisory' and btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 is now at current_stage='shadow', both flipped at the identical timestamp 2026-07-20T19:54:13+00:00 -- i.e. this Tier-3 decision was made and actioned about 12 hours before this /system-review session started, not 'sitting un-actioned' as I incorrectly flagged. items.title: De-noise the build-time dataset audit (62/86 manifests flagged nightly), then consider enforcement
items.description: Extract WHICH columns trip the dead-feature flag per manifest (FeatureAudit.name), classify expected-dead (optional side-streams a manifest doesn't use should NOT flag — the audit scores only manifest feature_columns, so investigate why base heads flag), add a per-manifest expected-dead whitelist or tighten thresholds, and once a flagged row is rare + real, flip the observe-only FLAGGED branch in run_training_cycle.sh to skip (enforce). An audit nobody reads is the same as no audit.

updates.note: PRIORITY RAISED — operator directive 2026-07-19 (see-something-say-something rule, PR #6956): this item is now the poster child for the normalization failure mode. 62/86 manifests alarming made the audit background noise, which concealed the ETH-xa dead-feature bug through weeks of soak. Fix shape: make the audit HIGH-PRECISION (alarm only on decision-relevant defects: dead/zero-variance features, label-coverage collapse, train/serve divergence) so that ANY alarm demands action, and wire it into the ml-review soak-integrity audit (skill updated in PR #6953). Target: alarms drop to near-zero baseline; an alarm becomes a stop-the-line signal, not wallpaper.

Re-validated 2026-07-22 with fresh data (the mandatory soak-integrity audit for this run): runtime_logs/trainer/dataset_audit.jsonl (671 total rows) — last 500 rows show 200/500 (40%) flagged, essentially the full manifest roster flagged repeatedly (BTC regime/direction manifests + utility baselines each appear flagged 8-9 times, i.e. every cycle in the file's history). This is down from the 2026-07-19 finding of 62/86 (~72%) manifests-per-night, so SOME improvement has occurred, but the de-noise/enforcement fix (expected-dead whitelist, FLAGGED->skip enforcement) described in this item has NOT yet shipped — every flagged row this session still reads 'observe-only, still training' in the cycle log, and the audit remains blanket rather than high-precision. Concrete diagnostic lead for whoever picks this up: sampled row for trade-outcome-lgbm-v1 shows 'killzone' and 'bias' columns at nan_fraction=1.0 tripping quarantine:true — these look like dataset-wide audited columns that may not even be in this manifest's own trainer_config.feature_columns (worth checking whether the audit scores the full dataset schema instead of just the manifest's declared feature list, per the original F3 hypothesis). Kept open, still Tier-1/P1 per the operator's 2026-07-19 priority raise.
Re-validated 07-26: dataset-audit de-noise still pending; the empty_dataset MES skips remain the visible noise. Carried.

PROGRESS 2026-07-26 (operator follow-up). Pulled live dataset_audit.jsonl via trainer-vm-diag: the roster is now 88 manifests, 22 flagged (25%) — already DOWN from the 62/86 (72%) that opened this item, thanks to the earlier categorical-false-positive fix (BL-20260718-AUDIT-CATEGORICAL-FALSEPOS). Classified the 22: (A) 8 are n_rows=0 EMPTY datasets flagging on LABEL (TCN heads, MES baselines, exit-policy-v1, corpus-ssl) — you cannot judge a dead feature or degenerate label on 0 rows, so this is a category error / pure noise in the dead-feature channel; (B) 13 flag purely on OPTIONAL side-stream feature families whose data source isn't wired for that head: fc_* (forecast), corpus_emb_*, open_interest_* (funding), ofi/vpin/order_imbalance/microprice (order-flow, DATA-BLOCKED per MB-20260613-002), parkinson/garman_klass/rogers_satchell/yang_zhang_vol, c_reg (D2b not real per MB-20260618-XA-D2B) — these are REAL 'the head trains on a dead feature block' findings, cross-referenced to already-tracked items, NOT noise to blanket-whitelist (that would re-blind the ETH-xa class); (C) 1 real degenerate label (prop-mission-policy-baseline-v0, 267 rows, MB-20260525-005). SHIPPED (this PR, ml/datasets/audit.py + scripts/ops/run_training_cycle.sh): n_rows=0 now classifies as a distinct `empty_dataset` category and is kept OUT of the dead-feature/degenerate-label `quarantine` alarm channel (surfaced instead as a separate `manifest_dataset_empty` cycle event), removing category (A) — the single biggest noise source — from the alarm without hiding it. The ETH-xa guard is UNTOUCHED: a dead feature in a NON-empty dataset still fully flags+quarantines (regression test added). Net: the alarm channel now fires only on real dead-feature/degenerate-label conditions in datasets that DID build. REMAINING (operator direction): categories (B)+(C) are genuine, already-tracked findings — deciding whether to (i) leave them as tracked/expected nightly flags, (ii) add a per-manifest 'expected-optional feature family' declaration so a soaking head's known-unwired side-stream doesn't alarm until its data source is live (a manifest-schema change), or (iii) flip FLAGGED->skip enforce, is a design/Tier-3 call. Recommend (ii) as the durable high-precision endpoint. Kept open pending that decision.

updates.by: claude (backlog-drain-tier1 session 2026-07-26, operator approved option a)
updates.note: OPTION (a) IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-26 (operator-approved). ml/datasets/audit.py now honours a per-manifest `trainer_config.expected_optional_features` declaration (exact names or fnmatch globs like `fc_*`): a flagged-dead column that matches is recorded in a new `expected_optional_dead` report field + marked `expected_optional:true` on the feature, but is kept OUT of `flags`/`quarantine` (the alarm channel). Default is EMPTY -> nothing is silenced unless a manifest EXPLICITLY opts a family out, so an UNDECLARED dead feature (the ETH-xa class) still fully alarms (regression test pins this: a declared `fc_*` is silenced while an undeclared `xa_peer` in the SAME manifest still quarantines). +6 audit tests. POPULATED the two highest-confidence, already-tracked not-yet-wired cases: (1) btc-regime-5m-lgbm-flow-v1 order-flow columns (ofi/ofi_zscore/vpin/order_imbalance/rel_spread_mean/microprice_dev) — 0.0 until the ict-orderflow-capture side-car accrues forward L2 (MB-20260604-002/MB-20260613-002, DATA-BLOCKED); (2) conviction-meta-{v1,base-btc-v1,emb-btc-v1} c_reg — the regime conviction lens is not real yet (MB-20260618-XA-D2B). Each manifest carries a comment saying to REMOVE the declaration once the source is wired (that's when a still-dead column becomes a real bug again). Verified all 4 manifests parse and the resolver reads the field. REMAINING per-head declarations (fc_*, corpus_emb_*, funding open_interest_*, parkinson/gk/rs/yz vol) are left for ml-review to add as each head's intent is confirmed — the mechanism is now in place. updates.note: CORRECTION + REAL FIX 2026-07-26. Operator pushed on WHY the not-yet-wired heads weren't accruing. Verified each column's live value via trainer-vm-diag (#7622-#7625) instead of trusting the manifest headers, and the earlier 'declare them all expected-optional' disposition was PARTLY WRONG — two of the three families were NOT 'awaiting a source', they were WIRED-BUT-BROKEN: (1) fc_* on btc-regime-15m-lgbm-fc-pcv-v2 audited 100% dead NOT because the forecast is missing (the nightly produces a fresh forecast side-stream, verified fresh on disk) but because build_funding_oi (now that ICT_BUILD_FUNDING_OI=1 is on) re-overwrote the SAME 15m v002 shard WITHOUT forecast_path minutes AFTER build_bybit_15m_fc joined it — a build-ordering clobber (15m data.jsonl mtime 05:20 > the 05:14 forecast build, fc_ret_med=0.0). FIXED: build_funding_oi's rebuild scoped to 1h only (both funding manifests are 1h; the 5m/15m rebuilds were pure waste and the 15m one destroyed the fc join). Filed MB-20260726-FC-CLOBBER (RESOLVED this PR). Removed the fc-pcv-v2 fc_* silence — a still-dead fc_* is a REAL alarm again. (2) funding_rate* is LIVE/populated (0.00010439) — silencing it was the ETH-xa over-silence mistake; DROPPED from funding-v1's declaration. Only open_interest_change/_zscore stay dead (~99.6% zero) because Bybit's OI-history endpoint serves only recent months, not the >=5y window — an upstream data-coverage limit, filed MB-20260726-OI-HISTORY-LIMIT, silenced as open_interest_* only. (3) corpus_emb_* IS genuinely unwired (no encoder producer, no timer) — declaration KEPT. fc-v1 (offline candidate on manual v004, not in the nightly cycle) declaration KEPT with a corrected comment. Lesson reinforced: 'not-yet-wired' vs 'wired-but-broken' must be verified per-column against live values before silencing — a header saying 'awaits X' can hide a clobber. items.title: MES 5m candle base is RTH-only (90 bars/day, 13:30-21:00Z) while the live head scores the full ~23h session -- caps RG4 labeling at ~35% and starves promotion power
items.source: WS-A MES RG4 re-read after the 07-19 base refresh: unlabeled stayed 1215/1863 despite fresh coverage through 07-17 20:55Z. Per-day diagnostic (trainer-diag #6984/#6985/#6986): datasets-out/market_raw/MES/5m/v002 has EXACTLY 90 bars/day, 13:30:00Z-20:55:00Z, zero intra-day gaps -- a US-RTH window -- while mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 logs ~255-260 shadow rows/day across the full CME session. 90/260 = 0.346 matches the labeled fraction 648/1863 = 0.348 exactly. items.description: Root-cause which layer forces RTH: scripts/ops/pull_mes_ibkr_history.sh passes use_rth=false to ml/datasets/percontract_pull.py (and adapters/ibkr_offvm.py defaults use_rth=False), yet the v002 rows (source=ibkr_offvm) are strictly 13:30-21:00Z. items.title: promotion-readiness sweep memory-thrashes the 6GB trainer (~5GB RSS, D-state, 0-byte outputs) -- inline compute_oos_edge over every shadow model in ONE process; needs the per-model subprocess isolation the training cycle got
items.source: Two identical thrash episodes on 2026-07-19, BOTH killed: (1) 12:37 launch, killed 14:55 after 2h18m at 4.94GB RSS/D-state with 0-byte cli_stdout.json; (2) 15:31 relaunch on parity-gate code (d068089), killed ~16:35 after >1h at 4.98GB RSS, same 0-byte outputs -- so the regression is NOT the parity code. Inputs are tiny (shadow log 43MB/53k rows, backfill 5.4MB, registry 4.3MB/91 models); the hog is ml/promotion/stage_guard.py::run_stage_guard calling compute_oos_edge(entry, datasets_root=...) INLINE for every shadow-stage entry -- each is a full purged-walk-forward retrain/eval (dataset load + LightGBM folds), all in one long-lived process on the 5.9GB box. Same failure class as BL-20260717-TRAINER-SINGLE-MANIFEST-OOM (fixed for the TRAINING cycle via per-manifest subprocesses + cgroup cap); the readiness sweep never got that treatment, and the roster/dataset growth (91 models; WS-B added ~10 symbols to datasets-out on 07-19) pushed it over the cliff. The 07-19 report was recovered by re-running WITHOUT --datasets-root (shadow models hold on oos_edge insufficient_data -- attribution/drift/stages still report).
items.description: Fix shape (mirror the training-cycle memfix): (a) run each compute_oos_edge in a bounded subprocess (fresh interpreter per model, or per-model batches) so peak RSS is one model's working set, not the fleet's accumulation; (b) put MemoryMax + MemorySwapMax=0 on ict-promotion-readiness.service (it has NO cgroup cap today -- only ict-trainer.service does) so a regression fails fast instead of D-state thrashing the whole box for hours; (c) consider making the unit's ExecStart pass --datasets-root only to a scoped oos-edge phase. Interim workaround (documented): run the sweep without --datasets-root for the daily report; oos_edge evidence comes from the single-model gate-check CLI on the head under review (which is where promotion packets are assembled anyway, per the M25 reframe).
items.resolution_criteria: BOTH must hold, measured not inferred: (1) MEMORY — a single head's compute_oos_edge peaks measurably under MemoryMax (4500 MiB) on the trainer, verified by /usr/bin/time -v on the largest shadow dataset on disk, not by reading the code; and (2) WALL CLOCK — a full-registry sweep WITH --datasets-root completes inside its timer window. Baseline to beat, from #10044: 5.19 GB and 5:35 for one head. ALTERNATIVELY the design is formally changed so oos_edge is per-head-at-gate-check-time only, the sweep drops --datasets-root by design, and every doc claiming a fleet-wide oos_edge sweep is corrected to match.

Re-check ONLY after a chunked/columnar CV load lands — and measure the WALL CLOCK too (5:35/head x 28 shadow heads = ~2.6 h on 1 OCPU is a second, independent blocker on daily scheduling).

FIXED (subprocess isolation, resolution-criteria branch 1). run_stage_guard now computes each shadow model's oos_edge in a FRESH subprocess via the new internal `python -m ml _oos-edge-one` worker (ml/promotion/stage_guard.py::_oos_edge_for_entry + ml/cli.py::_cmd_oos_edge_one), so the whole-registry sweep's peak RSS = one model's working set, not the fleet's accumulation. Fallback-to-None on any subprocess error keeps a per-model crash from aborting the sweep. run_promotion_readiness.sh PROMOREADY_OOS_EDGE default flipped off->on (sweep runs WITH --datasets-root again = real promote/hold/demote evidence in the daily report); the service unit's MemoryMax=4500M/MemorySwapMax=0 stays as a hard backstop (parts b already landed 2026-07-19). Unit-validated (worker registers, null-path, isolated signature); single-model compute proven bounded by today's gate-check runs (7610/7611 ran compute_oos_edge to completion, no OOM). Full-sweep-at-scale confirmation is the next daily ict-promotion-readiness.timer fire (post-merge). PR: system-review weekly branch.

REOPENED — the 2026-07-26 'resolved via subprocess isolation' does NOT hold. Live-confirmed 2026-07-27: with PROMOREADY_OOS_EDGE default ON, ict-promotion-readiness.service OOM-killed (Result=oom-kill) on both the 04:04Z scheduled run and an 08:49Z manual run (~5 min, no packet). ROOT CAUSE: ml/promotion/oos_edge.py:201 compute_oos_edge does rows=_load_jsonl(data_path) — materializes the ENTIRE dataset (market_features ~2.1e5 rows x many float cols, as Python dicts) for ONE head's CV, then _pooled_cv_metrics trains candidate+baseline on it. A SINGLE head's footprint exceeds MemoryMax=4500M, so per-head subprocess isolation (which only bounds fleet-accumulation) can't save it. INTERIM (shipped 2026-07-27): reverted PROMOREADY_OOS_EDGE default to OFF (restores the proven 07-25/26 packet-producing state; oos_edge evidence stays available per-head via `gate-check`). REAL FIX (this item): make oos_edge's CV dataset load memory-bounded — load only the manifest feature_columns + target + time column, as compact arrays/typed columns rather than full-row dicts, through _pooled_cv_metrics; then re-enable default ON only after a trainer live-verify shows the full sweep stays under the 4500M cap. Sibling of BL-20260715's attribution streaming fix (#7716), same materialization class.

MEMORY FIX SHIPPED (#7722): compute_oos_edge now projects the dataset load to only the trainer/evaluator-referenced columns via _load_jsonl(keep=), cutting a single head's rows-list footprint. ON-viability first measure (transient systemd-run scope, MemoryMax=4500M, PROMOREADY_OOS_EDGE=on) was INCONCLUSIVE — the pipe masked systemd-run's real exit and captured no /usr/bin/time -v RSS line, so it's unknown whether the ON sweep completed under the cap or OOM'd early. Re-measuring cleanly (explicit scope exit + time -v RSS + dmesg OOM check). Default stays OFF until a definitive under-cap result; then flip ON + resolve. oos_edge evidence remains available per-head via `gate-check`.

Interim workaround EXERCISED successfully in production (2026-08-01, #8254/#8257): per-model gate_check_candidates.sh over 2 heads WITH --datasets-root ran to completion on the 6GB box with no thrash (per-model process isolation = one model's working set at a time). [audit-0820] MEASURED at last — this criterion had been asserted for 24 days and never once measured, and the measurement REFUTES the natural reading of PR #7722. THE SEQUENCE MATTERS AND IS THE POINT: #7721 (a6ca3302) reverted this default to `off` on 2026-07-27, and #7722 (4d1d6663) — which added the memory fix, `keep=_referenced_columns(manifest)` on the oos_edge dataset load — merged THIRTEEN MINUTES LATER. Nothing ever went back to turn the flag on, so the fix has been deployed and inert for 24 days. That is this repo's build-and-abandon class in its purest observed form: the remedy shipped, the workaround stayed, and no artifact recorded that the two had crossed. THE MEASUREMENT (trainer-diag #10044, 2026-08-20): the projection IS present on the trainer (ml/promotion/oos_edge.py:247, grep-confirmed against the deployed tree at 220a9d42), and one head still does not fit. items.title: RESOLVED as FALSE ALARM: the "serving-parity skew" was the gate INSTRUMENT — score_fidelity coerced int features to float (_num) before predicting, shifting every re-score; live serving was byte-perfect all along

FIX: score_fidelity now predicts on the raw row exactly as logged (no coercion). The lightgbm==4.6.0 pin shipped earlier the same day (PR #7082 + pull-and-deploy) was NOT the cause but stays as good hygiene (equalized live/trainer stacks). NOTE: earlier MES + BTC/SOL "100% fidelity mismatch" reads carry the same instrument artifact — re-cert under the fixed instrument. A model retrained nightly on a GROWING dataset should drift slightly every run. Suspects: the fc-pcv dataset build is pinned/stale (not rebuilt with new rows), the trainer caches/skips when the dataset is unchanged, or the manifest trains on a frozen window. Consequence: the 'nightly retrain self-corrects drift' assumption in the drift-remediation playbook is FICTION for this head (and likely siblings — SOL fc-pcv shows std=0.0 over 3 runs; check the full fleet). Verify: compare the dataset build mtimes/row counts consumed by consecutive fc-pcv runs; check dataset_builds.jsonl for the market_features/BTCUSDT/15m family build cadence. Fix: ensure the nightly build actually appends fresh rows and the trainer consumes the updated version pin. NOT AFFECTED: the ADVISORY live vol-gate head btc-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 (v002, 0.2d fresh, metrics changing run-to-run) and the whole v002 fleet incl. every MES head — LIVE TRAINING IS HEALTHY for everything on the nightly-rebuilt datasets. MECHANISM: scripts/ops/build_trainer_datasets.sh rebuilds ONLY DATASET_VERSION=v002 (--overwrite) nightly; experiment-pinned versions (v5xx/v9xx/v001) freeze at build date, yet their manifests sit in the nightly train roster — burning no-op retrains and making cross_run_stability read as fake-perfect. WATCH (fresh ds but last-2 metrics identical, non-baseline): eth-regime-5m-lgbm-v1, sol-regime-15m-lgbm-v1, sol-regime-5m-lgbm-v1 — verify eval-window rounding vs genuine skip. FIX SHAPE: (a) cycle-level guard — skip retrain when the manifest's dataset mtime predates the last run, log 'dataset unchanged' loudly (kills silent no-ops + saves compute); (b) per-head decision to either add the pinned feature builds (fc/pcv variants) to the nightly build or take pinned-manifest heads out of the nightly roster.

NOT promoted — only the 5m head was operator-pre-approved. PARKED pending a design decision: the ML vol-verdict resolves the advisory head PER-SYMBOL (ml_vol_regime_for_symbol), so promoting a 2nd MES advisory head at a different timeframe raises a which-head-wins resolution question that needs answering before it would be safe/meaningful to promote. [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: The design question this item parked on IS answered in code: src/runtime/regime/ml_vol_verdict.py:341-368 `_advisory_entry_for_symbol` deterministically ranks a symbol's advisory heads — non-yz first, then the **15m** timeframe (the backtest clock), then shortest tf — and `ml_vol_regime_for_symbol` (line 371) resolves per-SYMBOL, not per-(symbol,timeframe). So multi-timeframe ambiguity has a defined winner. mes-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 is still shadow per the item's own 2026-07-26 re-validation (n=1204) and ml/configs/mes-regime-15m-lgbm-v2.yaml is not an advisory declaration. — PROPOSED CHANGE (Tier-3, operator decides one of two): (a) CLOSE — confirm the operator-pre-approved MES 5m advisory head is sufficient and record that a 2nd same-symbol head is not wanted; or (b) PROMOTE mes-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 shadow->advisory, explicitly accepting that `_advisory_entry_for_symbol`'s 15m preference would make the NEW head — not the operator-approved 5m head — the one that drives MES's live vol label, silently displacing it from the decision path. Option (b) must not be taken without stating that displacement; it is the substantive consequence the 'which-head-wins' question was hiding.

2026-08-16 (sysrev-0816): THE WHICH-HEAD-WINS QUESTION THIS ROW PARKED IS NOW ANSWERED, and the operator has decided. Answer: the resolution is DETERMINISTIC and the 15m head WOULD WIN. src/runtime/regime/ml_vol_verdict.py::_advisory_entry_for_symbol ranks the symbol's advisory heads by (is_yz, prefer_15m, tf_order) and takes sorted(...)[0]. The incumbent mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2 scores (0, 1, 5); a promoted mes-regime-15m-lgbm-v2 scores (0, 0, 15), which sorts FIRST because the resolver explicitly prefers the 15m timeframe as 'the backtest clock'. So promoting the 15m head does NOT add a second opinion -- it REPLACES which model drives MES's vol label at every timeframe, while leaving two heads at advisory with an implicit winner. OPERATOR DECISION 2026-08-16: do NOT promote yet -- compare the two heads head-to-head first. The reason is that no such comparison exists: the 15m head's gate-readiness was established on its OWN merits in isolation (2026-07-20 re-cert), and nothing has ever measured which of the two produces the better MES vol label. Swapping the model that governs a symbol's routing with no comparative evidence is the same shape as the tlt_pullback_1h near-miss the same day. WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS: either (a) a head-to-head on MES vol-label quality that picks a winner, after which promote AND demote the loser in one change so the registry shows ONE advisory head rather than two with a tie-break, or (b) a recorded decision that the 5m head is sufficient, which closes this row. Note the row's original framing -- 'define the per-symbol multi-timeframe advisory-head resolution' -- is partly satisfied: the resolution is DEFINED in code and is not ambiguous. What is missing is not a rule, it is evidence about which head should win under it. checked: src/runtime/regime/ml_vol_verdict.py, ml/registry-store/registry.jsonl via trainer relay #9645.

items.title: [M28][P4] Run the value-thesis backtest gate once FRED valuation-snapshot history accrues — AND first verify the soak is actually producing data
items.description:
Two-step follow-up so the M28 P4 decisive gate doesn't stall silently:
(1) VERIFY THE SOAK IS RUNNING: check (via diag relay) that runtime_logs/valuation_snapshots.jsonl on the live VM is accruing rows — the P3 tick (run_macro_thesis_tick) reads snapshots but the FRED fetch that WRITES them 'runs off-VM'; confirm that producer is actually scheduled/running and appending point-in-time rows (append-only, observed_at per revision). If it is NOT producing data, that is the real blocker to surface — wiring the FRED snapshot producer is the prerequisite, not the backtest.
(2) RUN THE GATE once there is enough history (aim for >= a few months across the seed universe): python scripts/macro/thesis_backtest_run.py --candles-dir <per-symbol daily-close CSVs> --rebalance-every 30 --horizon-days 30 --fee-frac <real> --carry-frac-per-day <roll/carry> --json out. The P4 gate: does thesis_conviction predict realized hit-rate (calibration_rank > 0), is mean_net_return positive NET of cost, and does edge_vs_baseline beat the naive all-long arm — OUT OF SAMPLE. Nothing graduates to live (P5 options expression, P6 c_macro overlay — both Tier-3) until this passes. Honor low-n honesty (a handful of wins is not significance).

items.title: [M28][P4-prereq] Wire the off-VM FRED valuation-snapshot producer (+ committed-path reader fallback) so P4 has point-in-time history
items.description: run_valuation_feed / fred_fetch_and_history exist, are FRED-validated, and are off-VM-guarded, but have NO scheduled caller. Recommended build (file-backed, money-VM socket-free, mirrors comms/reports + gpu_spend_ledger patterns): (1) a thin entrypoint scripts/macro/valuation_snapshot_produce.py that sets ICT_OFFVM_BUILD_HOST=1, calls fred_fetch_and_history(config) -> run_valuation_feed(...) to build append-only point-in-time rows (observed_at=fetch time; a revision is a NEW line), and appends/commits them to comms/macro/valuation_snapshots.jsonl; (2) a scheduled GitHub Actions cron (e.g. daily) that runs it and commits the rows — the live VM picks them up via ict-git-sync, no SSH write to the money box, no live-VM FRED socket; (3) teach valuation_store.snapshot_log_path (+ the P4 runner --snapshots) to prefer the committed comms/macro/ path when present, falling back to runtime_logs/. Keyless (FRED fredgraph.csv needs no key), so no operator secret. Seed series already in config/macro_valuation.yaml. Producer script + Actions cron are Tier-1 (offline tooling + CI); the reader fallback is a best-effort read-path change to a live module (argue Tier-1, board-flag). Nothing here touches an order path — P5/P6 stay Tier-3.

items.description: New milestone. Model a domain as stocks/flows/feedback-loops-with-delays; AI does system identification (ML fits structure/params/lags from point-in-time data), structure elicitation (LLM authors the causal-loop diagram from research text, data falsifies), and scenario generation (run forward -> scenario distributions conditioning thesis conviction/sizing). Phases P0(scope lock)->P1(engine+hand model)->P2(AI sysID)->P3(scenario soak, observe-only)->P4(decisive calibration+net-of-cost backtest vs M28 baseline)->P5(c_macro overlay, Tier-3)->P6(fleet self-model). items.title: setup-candidates-metalabel-xsym-yz-v1 range-vol estimators read DEAD despite being OHLC-computable — the dataset wasn't rebuilt on setup_candidates builder v2
items.description: The audit flags parkinson_vol/garman_klass_vol/rogers_satchell_vol/yang_zhang_vol as dead (nan) on setup-candidates-metalabel-xsym-yz-v1. Unlike the fc_*/corpus_emb_*/funding/order-flow side-streams (which await an external source), these four range-vol estimators are COMPUTED FROM each candidate's past-only OHLC window by setup_candidates builder v2 (the manifest header documents this + says to rebuild with --overwrite so the columns are present). OHLC is present, so dead range-vol columns mean the on-disk dataset was built on builder v1 (no range-vol emission) or the emission is broken. This is a REAL fixable build bug, deliberately NOT silenced via expected_optional_features. FIX: rebuild the xsym-yz setup_candidates dataset on builder v2 (--overwrite) and confirm the four range-vol columns populate; then re-audit. If they're STILL dead after a v2 rebuild, the estimator computation in the setup_candidates family is broken and needs a code fix.

items.description: The nightly build_bybit_15m_fc builds BTCUSDT 15m v002 market_features WITH the forecast side-stream joined (forecast_path -> fc_* populated). items.title: Bybit open-interest history only covers recent months — open_interest_change reads ~99.6% dead over the >=5y funding training window
items.description: The funding/OI side-stream IS wired (ICT_BUILD_FUNDING_OI=1) and funding_rate/_zscore/_abs_z populate correctly across the window. But Bybit's V5 open-interest-history endpoint (ccxt fetch_open_interest_history) only serves ~recent months regardless of the `since` cursor, while the funding manifests train on the rolling >=5y window (MARKET_START = 5 years ago). So open_interest_change / open_interest_change_zscore are 0.0 for the pre-OI-availability ~99% of rows — the audit correctly flags them dead. This is an upstream data-coverage limit, not a pipeline bug (silenced as open_interest_* only on btc-regime-1h-lgbm-funding-v1; funding_rate* left live). OPTIONS for whoever picks this up: (i) re-scope the funding manifests' dataset window to the OI-available window (a few months of 1h bars) so OI is dense — at the cost of a much shorter training set; (ii) source a deeper OI history from another provider; (iii) accept OI as a sparse recent-only feature and drop the OI columns from the funding manifests, keeping only funding_rate. The funding heads are research_only/offline (zero live-order impact), so this is not urgent. Also affects btc-regime-1h-lgbm-funding-svble-v1 (same 1h dataset).

items.source: The M16 backtest-augmentation live-holdout A/B (conviction-meta-v1-bt vs conviction-meta-v1) was graded on accuracy/macro-F1 from the trainer's default MulticlassClassificationEvaluator (relay #7782). Accuracy at a 0.5 threshold is a blunt metric for a P(win) RANKING/sizing model — a model can carry AUC ~0.56 while accuracy sits below the majority-class baseline.
items.title: M16 conviction A/B: matched-holdout AUC read (both models on identical live rows)
items.description: The A/B verdict was NEGATIVE on accuracy (v1-bt 0.5247 <= v1 0.5250, both below the ~0.64-0.66 majority-class baseline); conviction-meta-v1-bt stays candidate/observe-only. The rigorous cut NOT yet run: evaluate BOTH models on the IDENTICAL held-out live rows and compare AUC / log-loss (the metric the conviction stacker is actually used for — ranking/sizing, not 0.5-threshold classification). The current A/B used each model's own time_aware_holdout (n=385 union vs n=80 live-only), so the holdout row sets differ. Method: build the live conviction_meta dataset once (db_path pointed at the pulled trainer journal), take a fixed time-ordered live split, score v1-bt and v1 on the SAME eval rows, report AUC + log-loss + calibration by source. LOW priority + LOW expected value: the promotion verdict is very unlikely to flip (both at/below coin-flip on accuracy; augmentation gave no lift), so this is rigor/completeness, not a live decision — and the real bottleneck is the tiny live label pool (~400 rows), so also revisit only if that grows materially. Parent (resolved): BL-20260727-CONVICTION-UNION-NO-LIVE-ROWS (health-review-backlog). Recipe + verdict: docs/research/m30-to-m16-integration-backbone-DESIGN.md sec 5.4/6.

items.opened_by: claude (audit session, W0 morning cycle check — routed from the first training_staleness_summary)
items.source: First run of the P1 staleness reporter (scripts/ops/manifest_training_staleness.py), trainer cycle of 2026-08-01T05:13Z (trainer-diag #8213): scanned 89 manifests, 3 stale, all 3 never_trained, 0 unresolvable, threshold 7d. updates.note: Weekly /system-review: confirmed live in both 08-01 cycles — training_staleness_summary {scanned:89, stale:3, never_trained:3}; the 3 are mes-execution-quality / mes-setup-quality / mes-trade-outcome-winrate baselines, 64.6d old, skipped every cycle since landing (the new P1 escalation is doing its job). Recommendation for next /ml-review: RETIRE the three manifests unless someone commits to building their datasets — 64 days of silent skip is evidence nobody needs them; retiring also de-noises the staleness summary.

OPERATOR DECIDED: BUILD (chat 2026-08-01). All 3 dataset families built MES-scoped on the trainer (issue #8256): datasets-out/{execution_quality,setup_labels,trade_outcomes}/MES/all/v001 — exactly the family/symbol_scope/version the manifests pin. Verify the 08-02 00:55Z nightly cycle trains mes-execution-quality-baseline-v0 / mes-setup-quality / mes-trade-outcome-winrate-baseline-v0 (staleness summary should drop never_trained 3 -> 0); resolve this row on that evidence.

BUILD EXECUTED, ROOT CAUSE REFRAMED. Operator chose 'build'; all 3 dataset families built MES-scoped (#8256) and an immediate verification train dispatched (#8259). Result: every build 'succeeds' but writes 0 rows -> `ml train` skips {reason: empty_dataset} -> still 0 registered runs. Root cause chased to ground (#8260/#8262/#8263): the trainer's full journal pull (698MB, fresh) contains ZERO trades with symbol LIKE '%MES%' in ANY status, and the live audit shows mes_trend_long_1d evaluating healthily every tick on fresh data (close 7519.25 inside Donchian channel [7323.25, 7632.0], regime trending ADX 25.2, 'no breakout - non-actionable') - i.e. MES has NEVER opened a trade in ~65 days because the long-only 1d Donchian-24 breakout never triggered. The datasets are HONESTLY empty: these 3 manifests are trade-derived (trade_outcomes/setup_labels/execution_quality) and cannot train until MES accrues closed trades. The dataset dirs have been empty since May 22; the nightly built an empty setup_labels v002 today - so 'build' was never the missing step. DECISION REFRAMED for the operator: (a) keep manifests + teach the staleness sweep an 'awaiting_source_trades' state (source-empty != build-missing) so the alarm stops firing nightly on an honest wait - Tier-1 trainer change; or (b) retire the 3 manifests and recreate when MES has traded (they are trivial per-strategy baselines). Either kills the alarm-fatigue; leaving as-is re-alarms nightly on a condition nobody can act on.

TRAINED VIA BACKTEST BACKFILL (operator-directed: use the S-MLOPT-S7 pipeline instead of waiting for live MES trades). Chain (#8316/#8318): backtest_trend.py config-exact to mes_trend_long_1d (donchian 30, atr 14/2.5, trail 3.0, long-only) over data/ES_F_1d.csv (2514 daily bars 2016-2026, ES=F as the standard MES index proxy) -> 26 trades (wr 65.4%, net +24.9R, positive 9 of 11 years - incidentally fresh validation of the strategy itself, and confirms why live MES never fired: ~2.6 entries/yr) -> record_harness_trades into a schema-bootstrapped TEMP db (is_backtest=1, never the journal) -> trade_outcomes v001 + setup_labels v002 rebuilt with include_backtest=true (26 rows each) -> BOTH TRAINED + REGISTERED: mes-trade-outcome-winrate-baseline-v0 (f1 0.75, n_eval 5) and mes-setup-quality-baseline-v0 (mae 1.12, n_eval 5), both at shadow. DISCLOSED + CORRECTED: the first pass (#8316) accidentally ran on 5m bars (bad file pick) producing 552 wrong-timeframe trades; temp db was rebuilt from scratch and both models retrained on the corrected 1d data - the 5m-artifact run remains in run history only. REMAINING: (1) mes-execution-quality-baseline-v0 is the sole never-trained manifest left - entry_slippage_bps is a LIVE-execution measurement a backtest cannot produce; decide retire vs awaiting_source_trades alarm state for that ONE. (2) The nightly cycle rebuilds these datasets journal-only (no include_backtest) and will overwrite them empty; the REGISTERED runs persist and never_trained stays satisfied, but a refresh requires re-running this backfill - consider pinning the backtest-augmented build into the cycle if these baselines earn keep.

OPERATOR DECISIONS EXECUTED (chat 2026-08-02): (1) mes-execution-quality KEPT, waiting for live MES fills - not retired. The staleness sweep gained an operator-accepted-wait state: a never-trained manifest whose notes carry 'training-wait: awaiting_source_trades - <reason>' now reports the non-alarming manifest_awaiting_source status (+ awaiting_source summary counter) instead of the nightly manifest_untrained_stale alarm; the marker is in the manifest's notes (the manifest loader is a strict dataclass - a new top-level key would break ml.manifest.from_dict). A trained-then-stale model still alarms; removing the marker restores the alarm. (2) Backtest-augmented MES builds PINNED into the nightly: build_trainer_datasets.sh now merges live MES journal rows (zero today; future fills join automatically) + the standing datasets-out/backtest_trades_mes.db into a scratch db and rebuilds the MES-scoped trade_outcomes + setup_labels with include_backtest=true each cycle - so the datasets stop being clobbered empty by the journal-only builds. Missing backtest db -> explicit skipped row pointing at the backfill runbook, never silent. VERIFY on the 2026-08-03 00:55Z cycle: MES-scoped builds report row_count 26, staleness summary reads never_trained 0 / awaiting_source 1. (3) BTC v2 drift re-check moved UP to Sunday 2026-08-03 ~18:00Z (operator: crypto is 24/7 - the Monday date was my conflation with the SLV market-hours wait); wake armed.

NIGHTLY PIN VERIFIED — SPLIT RESULT, clobber found + fixed (trainer-diag #8433, cycle of 2026-08-03). PASS half: the merge step ran ('mes merged db: live=0 backtest=26', 05:01:00Z) and trade_outcomes/MES/all/v002 rebuilt backtest-augmented (row_count 26, build_params include_backtest:true + exclude_fabricated_pnl:true, sha 61aba824). The cycle's manifest_untrained_stale events list ONLY the 3 btc-tcn manifests + exit-policy-v1 — no MES manifest alarms, so the registered runs + the awaiting_source_trades waiver on mes-execution-quality are both holding (its skip is now the quiet {reason: empty_dataset} cycle row, not a staleness alarm). FAIL half: setup_labels/MES/all/v002 read row_count 0, generated 05:12:56Z with build_params {r_cap, risk_pct, symbol} only — the PRE-EXISTING build_mes_setup_labels() fallback helper (added 2026-06 so mes-setup-quality skips cleanly instead of FileNotFound-failing) runs LATER in the same script from the MES market-data section and its plain-journal build (0 live MES rows) OVERWROTE the augmented 26-row build from 12 minutes earlier. mes-setup-quality skipped {empty_dataset} this cycle; no permanent harm (the 2026-08-02 registered run persists — never_trained stays 0) but every future retrain would skip until fixed. FIXED same session (Tier-1): build_mes_setup_labels() now suppresses its rebuild (with an explicit skipped emit) whenever a non-empty MES setup_labels dataset is already present, keeping its original FileNotFound-guard role for the no-data case. Verify on the 2026-08-04 cycle: setup_labels/MES/all/v002 row_count 26 surviving to cycle end + the new skipped emit in the build log. RESOLVE this row on that evidence.

RESOLVED — the full chain verified working end-to-end on the 2026-08-04 cycle, twice in one day (trainer-diag #8451). Both runs (00:59Z nightly + 05:00Z catch-up) show the designed sequence: 'mes merged db: live=1 backtest=26' -> setup_labels/MES/all/v002 rebuilt augmented (row_count 26, build_params include_backtest:true + exclude_fabricated_pnl:true, sha 0ed8a5a6 >= the #8434 fix) -> ~30 min later the NEW suppression emit fires ('non-empty MES setup_labels dataset already present ... plain-journal fallback rebuild suppressed') instead of the clobber. data.jsonl reads 26 lines on disk AFTER cycle end for both families. The 02:12Z cycle TRAINED + REGISTERED both baselines as manifest_ok (mes-setup-quality-baseline-v0 run 20260804T021217Z, mes-trade-outcome-winrate-baseline-v0 run 20260804T021218Z) — no more empty_dataset skip. mes-execution-quality skips quietly per the awaiting_source_trades waiver (its execution_quality dataset is honestly empty until MES accrues CLOSED live fills with slippage measurements — that wait is the operator-accepted state, not this row's scope). NOTE: the merge marker reads live=1 — a live MES journal row now exists (was 0 throughout this saga) and the pin picked it up automatically, exactly the 'future fills ride along' design; the trade itself will surface through the normal trade notifications/reviews. All three original manifests are now either trained+registered (2) or in the accepted awaiting_source state (1): nothing left to drive here.

items.title: The 'exit_head_ml only works on ict_scalp' read was formed entirely on NO-TAKE-PROFIT books -- the first round run at live-parity TP returned a non-scalp candidate at equal AUC
items.source:
The standing read, recorded on the ict_scalp_sol_5m coverage cell, is 'all 5 surviving candidates are ict_scalp; every non-scalp family in the re-run is honest_negative'. It is the basis of the operator-queued question 'is exit_head_ml scalp-family-scoped?'.

On 2026-08-14 m20_exit_head_round.py was found STRUCTURALLY unable to pass a take-profit cap (BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-ROUNDS-CANNOT-MODEL-LIVE-TP): it called base_args positionally so tp_cap_pct defaulted to 0.0, and its argparse had no --tp-cap-pct at all. Measured: 11 of 13 audited round dirs contain ZERO take-profit exits over full populations (n=100..1992). So EVERY non-scalp honest_negative behind the scalp-scoping read was measured on a book production does not run.

The first round built after the fix, at live parity, returned trend_donchian_eth_prop as a CANDIDATE -- n_oos=902, auc=0.6138, beats_actual=20/24, beats_hard=16/24 -- against ict_scalp_sol_5m's auc=0.6149 on n_oos=800. That is the first non-scalp E1 candidate.

WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT. It is NOT a like-for-like counterexample and must not be cited as 'donchian passes too': the two are on different geometries and therefore different populations. What it establishes is that the scalp-scoping read rests on geometry-conditioned evidence and has never been tested at the geometry production actually runs. One leg is not that test.
items.resolution_criteria: Observable: the non-scalp legs that returned honest_negative in the pre-fix E1 re-run are re-run at live-parity TP (the driver now DEFAULTS to it, so this is a re-run and not a code change), and the scalp-scoping question is answered against that population -- either 'the read holds at correct geometry' or 'it does not'. The comparison must state its geometry on BOTH sides; a mixed-geometry table would reproduce the exact error this row exists to prevent. Scale note: this is a fleet-wide re-run and the DISPOSITION of anything it promotes is Tier-3. NOT resolution: treating the single trend_donchian_eth_prop candidate as having settled it in either direction.
evidence: docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json -- ict_scalp_sol_5m/exit_head_ml ref (the scalp-scoping read); trend_donchian_eth_prop/exit_head_ml ref (the new candidate + this caveat)
BL-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-ROUNDS-CANNOT-MODEL-LIVE-TP -- the driver defect and the 11-round audit
runtime_logs/m20_exit_head/prop_1h -- first live-parity round, _round_meta.tp_geometry=live_parity, 95 take-profit exits across its two legs
items.tier: 1 (the re-run; any promotion it argues for is Tier-3)

updates.note: [sysrev-0816 2026-08-16] re-validated this run: Substantially advanced within two days of opening, but the resolution criterion is not fully met. The driver defect is fixed (live parity is now the DEFAULT with a _round_meta geometry stamp; the first round at that default emitted 95 take-profit exits as the positive control) and 20 non-scalp legs now carry `tp_geometry: live_parity` in docs/research/exit-refinement-coverage.json (updated_at 2026-08-15) from the 2026-08-14/15 re-sweeps: trend_donchian 1h/eth/sol via relay #9206, the 1d pullback fleet via round pullback_1d_20260814T212317Z (relays #9358/#9366), and the 1h equity legs via relay #8921. The scoping question itself is ANSWERED against that population — a non-scalp leg cleared at live parity (trend_donchian_eth_prop passed_unshipped, auc 0.6138, n_oos 902) and trend_donchian_eth reads `shipped`, so 'exit_head_ml only works on ict_scalp' does NOT hold at correct geometry. What remains: SIX non-scalp legs still rest on pre-fix no-TP rounds with tp_geometry null — eth_pullback_2h, xrp_pullback_2h, ada_pullback_2h, eth_pullback_prop_2h (all 2026-07-12/13 round-3 refs) and trend_donchian_xrp_4h, trend_donchian_ada_4h (2026-07-12 round-2 refs), each still graded honest_negative on a book the live system never trades. — Not blocked on a decision — blocked on trainer compute I cannot dispatch from this checkout. TRIGGER: re-run scripts/research/m20_exit_head_round.py (which now defaults to live parity) on those six legs and record the resulting statuses WITH their geometry stamp on both sides of any comparison; a mixed-geometry table would reproduce the exact error this row exists to prevent. Downgrading severity because the load-bearing claim — that the scalp-scoping read is geometry-conditioned — is now demonstrated rather than suspected; what is left is completing the comparison population. NOT resolution: treating the single trend_donchian_eth_prop candidate as settling the question. Note also that the disposition of anything the re-run promotes is Tier-3.

items.title: Trainer disk at 93.5% (3.15 GB free) with the dataset GC measured as able to reclaim only 0.09 GB — the banner is firing and the named remedy does not work
items.detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-21 from /api/bot/ml/status disk: {free_gb: 3.15, total_gb: 48.28, used_gb: 45.13, used_pct: 93.5, measured: true}. /api/bot/notifications carries the trainer_disk_low warning banner (since 06:38Z).

The banner's own detail says the remedy does not apply: 'the dataset garbage collector is NOT the remedy: measured 2026-08-20 it reclaims 0.09 GB of 115 version dirs (111 held by 41 manifest pins)'. So 111 of 115 dataset versions are pinned by manifests and cannot be collected. That means the disk problem is a MANIFEST-PIN problem, not a retention problem, and no existing tool addresses it. Related already-open: BL-20260820-TRAINER-DATASET-GC-HAS-NO-CALLER, BL-20260820-TRAINER-DISK-THRESHOLDS-UNCALIBRATED.

A full trainer disk stops dataset builds and training cycles, and the trainer's own systemd state reports green throughout — which is exactly the condition that produced MB-20260821-CYCLE-TRAINED-ZERO-AND-SEVEN-MANIFESTS-STALE if it worsens.
items.why_it_matters: 3.15 GB of headroom against a build tree that has been growing, with the only named remedy measured at 0.09 GB of relief. This has a deadline attached to it whether or not anyone sets one.
items.next_action: Tier-1 first: measure what the 41 pinning manifests actually need — how many pins are held by manifests that are themselves stale or permanently refusing (see MB-20260821-CYCLE-TRAINED-ZERO-AND-SEVEN-MANIFESTS-STALE). Retiring a refusing manifest releases its pins. Tier-2 for the operator if that is insufficient: grow the trainer volume or move the dataset tree.
